title.raw: Austria preview: Antonelli's streak is broken, and the title race is open again
title.rendered: Austria preview: Antonelli’s streak is broken, and the title race is open again

content.raw:
For five races, the 2026 season had one simple shape: Kimi Antonelli won, and everyone else arranged themselves behind him. At Barcelona that shape broke — though not how anyone expected. Lewis Hamilton took a long-awaited maiden win for Ferrari, while Antonelli's afternoon ended in retirement four laps from home: his Mercedes shut down moments after he had fought past teammate George Russell for second. (race report, Formula1.com)

Where the title actually stands

One retirement does not undo five wins. Antonelli still leads the drivers' standings on 156 points; Hamilton's victory lifts him to second, 41 behind, with Russell a further nine back in third. Mercedes, on six wins, keep a commanding lead in the constructors' table. (standings via The Race)

But it was Antonelli's first retirement of the season, on a brutal day of seven DNFs, and it blew a title race that had started to look settled back open. Barcelona also made history of a gentler kind: Hamilton, Russell and Norris formed the first all-British Formula 1 podium since Jackie Stewart, Graham Hill and John Surtees in 1968. (Sky Sports)

What the Red Bull Ring asks

The Austrian Grand Prix is round eight, and the circuit is nothing like the one that just bit Antonelli: one of the shortest laps on the calendar, a quick blast of long full-throttle climbs and heavy braking zones strung across an Alpine hillside. It rewards power-unit efficiency and clean traction out of the slow corners, and punishes a car that can't put its energy down. Lap time is cheap here, so the gaps between the front-runners are thin and a single lock-up is expensive.

It is also the front half of a back-to-back: Silverstone and the British Grand Prix follow on 3-5 July, run to the sprint format. Two weekends, two very different tests, and a championship leader who needs to show Barcelona was a blip. (2026 calendar, Formula1.com)

Three things to watch

  • Antonelli's response. Five straight wins, then a cruel late DNF — how the 19-year-old bounces back will say more about his title bid than the streak did.
  • Ferrari on merit. Hamilton's first win in red came on a perfectly-timed Virtual Safety Car gamble; a victory on raw pace would turn a great day into a genuine campaign.
  • The Mercedes intramural. Russell and Hamilton are split by nine points in the fight for second — two cars chasing the same prize, with team priorities waiting to be tested.

Lights out at the Red Bull Ring is Sunday 28 June. Full session times and standings live on the Paddock F1 page.

title.raw: Russell holds off Verstappen in Austria — and the data shows where it was won
title.rendered: Russell holds off Verstappen in Austria — and the data shows where it was won

content.raw:
George Russell answered every question the Red Bull Ring asked — and then had to survive a nervous finish to make it stick. The Mercedes driver controlled the 2026 Austrian Grand Prix from pole, but a charging Max Verstappen turned a ten-second lead into a 1.6-second nail-biter by the flag, with Kimi Antonelli a further four tenths back in third after the freshest-tyre stint of the leading trio.

How the race ran

Russell led throughout, managing two sets of tyres through a scorching afternoon, while Verstappen — recovering from fifth on the grid after a late qualifying crash (Formula1.com) — carved his way forward. Two Virtual Safety Cars broke up the afternoon: the first when Carlos Sainz stopped with an electrical failure on lap 25, the second when Alex Albon dislodged a Turn 3 bollard on lap 52. There was no full Safety Car — but there was plenty going on behind the leader.

What the data says

The race turned on strategy, not pace. Three drivers gambled on a three-stop — Hamilton, Leclerc and Gasly — and all three came off worse for it. Hamilton's is the cautionary tale. Ferrari called him in late for his middle stop, so he ran an extra lap before diving in — but he still made it under the lap-25 Virtual Safety Car, so the stop itself was cheap. The mistake was the tyre: a set of used softs, fitted off hards barely a dozen laps old that were still in good shape. In track temperatures near 50°C the softs simply went off, while the harder rubber he'd ditched would have lasted. A third stop on lap 42 sealed it — and despite pace that had him in podium contention, Hamilton came home fifth, half a minute back. Leclerc's three-stop went the same way: second on the grid to eighth, the day's biggest loser.

Verstappen's second place was the drama of the afternoon — and a lesson in covering the undercut. Russell made his final stop on lap 43; Red Bull left Verstappen out until lap 49, and that late call handed Russell a cushion of around ten seconds (Motorsport.com, Sky Sports). But the same delay put Verstappen on the fresher rubber, and he made it count: through the closing stint he was comfortably the quicker car, chipping more than a second a lap off the gap and filling Russell's mirrors with Red Bull. He ran out of laps at 1.6 seconds. Over the full race, Paddock's median-pace read had the leading three covered by barely a tenth — but in those final laps Verstappen had the clear edge, and had Red Bull covered Russell's stop, the closing laps might have been a fight for the win rather than a recovery to second.

Antonelli had the quickest final stint of anyone. Stopping latest of the leaders for the freshest tyres, he set the race's fastest lap — a 1:10.374 — and very nearly pinched second on the last lap, crossing the line just 0.375s behind Verstappen, the podium covered by under two seconds.

Three things we learned

  • The two-stop was king. Fifteen of the eighteen finishers made just two stops; every three-stop gamble backfired in the Spielberg heat.
  • Cover the undercut, or pay for it. It was a late final stop, not a pace deficit, that kept Verstappen from fighting Russell for the win.
  • Cadillac has work to do. Both cars were gone inside four laps with brake trouble — a chastening afternoon for the grid's newest team.

Where it leaves the title

Antonelli still leads, on 171 points, but Russell's win cut the gap to 40 and lifted him past Hamilton into second. The fight behind is tighter still — Piastri, Norris and Leclerc covered by a single point.

Every stop, stint and overtake from Austria is broken down in Paddock's Race Story, and the full standings are live on the Paddock F1 page.

title.raw: British Grand Prix 2026 preview: a sprint, a home crowd, and a title race turned upside down
title.rendered: British Grand Prix 2026 preview: a sprint, a home crowd, and a title race turned upside down

content.raw:
Round 9 takes Formula 1 to Silverstone for a sprint weekend, with lights out at 15:00 BST on Sunday 5 July. Five British drivers, a brand-new breed of car, and a championship nobody predicted — here's the lay of the land.

The title picture

Kimi Antonelli didn't just adapt to F1's 2026 rules — he ran away with them. The Mercedes driver leads on 171 points, 40 clear of team-mate George Russell and 46 up on Lewis Hamilton, and Mercedes have won seven of eight races, leading Ferrari by 98 in the constructors'.

But the gap is shrinking. Antonelli's five-win streak (China, Japan, Miami, Canada, Monaco) ended with a DNF in Spain, and a scrappy Austria left him third — where Russell pounced to end his own winless run and arrive at his home race with the momentum.

The strangest line on the sheet: reigning world champion Lando Norris sits fifth. McLaren, dominant on the way to his 2025 crown, have slipped to third — behind only Mercedes and Ferrari — in the first year of the new rules. Norris is also the defending British GP winner, so a repeat would be some upset.

A very British Silverstone

Five home drivers line up: Russell (P2), Hamilton (P3), Norris (P5), Oliver Bearman (Haas) and rookie Arvid Lindblad (Racing Bulls) — the most British drivers on the grid in over 20 years. Russell is many pundits' pick after Austria. Hamilton — a record nine-time Silverstone winner — chases a 10th, with Ferrari bringing a revised active rear wing (the "Macarena") and a low-drag diffuser to a circuit that will test their power-unit deficit.

No DRS, new questions

2026 scrapped DRS. In its place: active aero (the wings flip between "Corner" and "Straight" mode) plus an "Overtake" mode that hands a battery boost to any driver within a second of the car ahead. Silverstone's flat-out corners barely let the cars recharge — Max Verstappen said the energy rules make the place feel "like a different track." His Red Bull took second in Austria, its best result of 2026; whether that pace holds at high-speed Silverstone is one of the weekend's big unknowns. (Driver-market chatter around Verstappen also rumbles on — treat it as paddock rumour for now.)

The format & conditions

It's Silverstone's first sprint since 2021 — just one practice session before it counts:

  • Fri 3 Jul — FP1 12:30 · Sprint Qualifying 16:30
  • Sat 4 Jul — Sprint 12:00 · Qualifying 16:00
  • Sun 5 Jul — Grand Prix 15:00 (52 laps)

(All times BST.) Unusually for Silverstone, it should stay warm and dry all weekend — into the mid-20s °C with near-zero rain, Saturday the windiest day. Pirelli brought its hardest tyres (C1–C3), pointing to a one-stop race.

What to watch

  • Can Russell turn home momentum into a first Silverstone win — and dent Antonelli's lead?
  • Does Red Bull's Austria form (Verstappen P2) carry to a very different circuit?
  • Ferrari's upgrades versus their straight-line weakness — and Hamilton's shot at a record-extending 10th home win.
  • Sprint points: eight are on offer Saturday, enough to quietly reshuffle the top of the table.

Lights out, Sunday 15:00 BST.

title.raw: Leclerc ends the drought as Silverstone descends into chaos — and Ferrari hit 250
title.rendered: Leclerc ends the drought as Silverstone descends into chaos — and Ferrari hit 250

content.raw:
Silverstone promised a Mercedes coronation and delivered a Ferrari resurrection. Charles Leclerc won a British Grand Prix that unravelled into late chaos and finished, anticlimactically, behind the Safety Car — but nothing could dull the headline. It was Leclerc's first win since the 2024 United States Grand Prix, his ninth in F1, his first at Silverstone, and, fittingly, Ferrari's 250th victory in Formula 1 — scored 75 years after the Scuderia's very first, on this same Northamptonshire tarmac, in 1951.

A pole that turned to heartbreak

It should have been Kimi Antonelli's day. The championship leader arrived on a high — Sprint pole had gone to Lewis Hamilton on Saturday morning, but Antonelli won the 17-lap Sprint to stretch his title lead to 43 points, then put it on pole for the Grand Prix with a 1:28.111, edging Leclerc by 0.175s with Hamilton third and a recovering George Russell fourth after an early spin at Luffield.

Then Sunday happened. Leclerc launched brilliantly, slipping ahead with Hamilton as Antonelli bogged slightly off the line. The Italian clawed his way back to second and briefly led when Leclerc pitted — but on lap 41 his car cried enough, Mercedes pointing to a left-front wheel-shield failure, compounded by a five-second track-limits penalty. From a probable win, Antonelli tumbled to 16th, out of the points, a fastest lap (1:31.777) his only souvenir. His championship lead, 43 points on Saturday night, was gone to just 25 by Sunday evening.

Verstappen, the Safety Car, and shades of 2021

The decisive blow came on lap 48. Max Verstappen, running a strong third and eyeing the podium, spun into the gravel at Stowe — the latest chapter in a recurring Red Bull problem he later called "frustrating and painful." His beached car brought out the Safety Car, and the race never went green again. Amid confusion over lapped cars and a false promise that the Safety Car would peel in — the FIA later blamed a software error that flashed an incorrect message — the finish carried unmistakable echoes of Abu Dhabi 2021, only this time the order simply froze.

Russell steals second at home

For George Russell it was a home race of two halves. A slow puncture had dropped him to seventh and seemingly out of the podium fight; Antonelli's failure and Verstappen's crash dragged him back into it, and by staying out while others pitted under the Safety Car he vaulted Lewis Hamilton for second. He was pointedly unimpressed with his own afternoon — but a home rostrum, and 18 points clawed back on his runaway teammate, will have softened it.

Hamilton completed the podium the hard way: a five-second penalty for a false start, then a post-race summons for a yellow-flag infringement that earned only a reprimand. Third on home soil, in red, he took it. Lando Norris salvaged McLaren's difficult weekend in fourth, while teammate Oscar Piastri never recovered from lap-one front-wing damage and trailed home 11th, out of the points.

The rest of the day

Behind the leaders, Isack Hadjar led Red Bull's charge to fifth, and Racing Bulls banked a double score through Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad in sixth and seventh — enough to close to within a single point of Alpine, whose Franco Colapinto and Pierre Gasly took ninth and tenth around Gabriel Bortoleto's Audi in eighth. Carlos Sainz's promising run ended pointless in 12th after a Safety Car breach cost him a lap. Verstappen, Alex Albon and Nico Hülkenberg were the retirements.

Top ten: 1. Leclerc (Ferrari), 2. Russell (Mercedes), 3. Hamilton (Ferrari), 4. Norris (McLaren), 5. Hadjar (Red Bull), 6. Lawson (Racing Bulls), 7. Lindblad (Racing Bulls), 8. Bortoleto (Audi), 9. Colapinto (Alpine), 10. Gasly (Alpine).

Where it leaves us

Antonelli still leads the championship, but a 43-point cushion is now 25, and the pressure — from his own teammate — is suddenly real. Ferrari, meanwhile, leave Silverstone with a landmark win and a driver reborn: "It feels incredible," said Leclerc. "To win after the last few weekends that have been particularly difficult…" The sentence trailed off, but the message didn't.

The season takes a weekend off and returns at the Belgian Grand Prix on 17–19 July — Spa, where chaos needs no invitation.

title.raw: Sachsenring, the title filter: Martín leads by seven as Márquez hunts a tenth
title.rendered: Sachsenring, the title filter: Martín leads by seven as Márquez hunts a tenth

content.raw:
MotoGP reaches the halfway point of its 2026 season at the Sachsenring this weekend, and it does so as a genuine four-way fight. Just 40 points cover the top five riders, and only 25 separate the top four — and for the first time all season, it is Jorge Martín who leads them. Germany is the last race before the summer break, on a circuit that has answered to one man for the best part of a decade. The paddock has a name for the weekend: a title filter.

Martín in front — for now

Martín arrives on 193 points, seven clear of his Aprilia team-mate Marco Bezzecchi, having taken the championship lead for the first time this year at Assen — where Bezzecchi crashed out of the lead for a third straight weekend without a score. Behind them the pressure never lets up: Fabio Di Giannantonio (177) and breakout rookie Ai Ogura (168) are both still inside 25 points of top spot. It is the tightest the table has been all season, and a weekend of two races — Saturday's Sprint and Sunday's Grand Prix — can rewrite it entirely before the break. The current table is on the MotoGP standings tab.

Márquez and the fortress

No Sachsenring preview can look past Marc Márquez. The reigning champion has won here nine times in the premier class — every year from 2013 to 2019, again in 2021, and last season — and the circuit's near-endless left-handers have long made him the favourite before a wheel turns. Yet he comes to Germany only fifth, 40 points down, chasing a tenth Sachsenring victory that would haul him back into a fight he cannot yet lead. He has also spoken candidly this season about the mental toll of a seventh operation on his arm. If anyone can bend this title filter, it is the man who owns the place.

Ogura, chasing history

Ogura turns up fresh from a maiden MotoGP win at Assen — the first for a Japanese rider since Makoto Tamada in 2004. No rider from Japan has led the premier-class standings in 51 years, and none has ever won back-to-back premier-class races. Ogura, remarkably, is within range of both.

A depleted grid

The entry list tells its own story before the lights go out. Johann Zarco misses the round after a heavy Barcelona crash left him with cruciate-ligament damage, a torn meniscus and a fractured fibula; 40-year-old Cal Crutchlow — a three-time Sachsenring podium finisher — stands in again at LCR Honda. Maverick Viñales is still short of strength in a troublesome right shoulder. The Sachsenring rewards the fully fit, and several on this grid are anything but.

The circuit

At 3.671 km the Sachsenring is one of the shortest laps of the year, and among the most singular: roughly 80% of it is spent on the side of the tyre, almost all of it turning left. Its signature is the 'Waterfall' — a 21-metre drop into the long left-hander that feeds the back straight, taken almost blind at close to 180 mph. Outright engine power counts for little here; corner speed, front-end confidence and tyre management decide it.

What's at stake

With big points on offer in both the Sprint and the Grand Prix, and a title fight this compressed, every session before the shutdown matters — momentum banked at the Sachsenring has to last a month. Session times in your local zone, the full schedule and results as they land are all on the German Grand Prix weekend page.

The lights go out for the Grand Prix on Sunday; after that, MotoGP scatters for the summer — and whoever leads Germany out gets to enjoy the break the most.

Just 40 points cover the top five riders, and only 25 separate the top four — and for the first time all season, it is Jorge Martín who leads them. Germany is the last race before the summer break, on a circuit that has answered to one man for the best part of a decade. The paddock has a name for the weekend: a title filter.

Martín in front — for now

Martín arrives on 193 points, seven clear of his Aprilia team-mate Marco Bezzecchi, having taken the championship lead for the first time this year at Assen — where Bezzecchi crashed out of the lead for a third straight weekend without a score. Behind them the pressure never lets up: Fabio Di Giannantonio (177) and breakout rookie Ai Ogura (168) are both still inside 25 points of top spot. title.raw: Belgian Grand Prix preview: F1 returns to Spa with the title fight tightening
title.rendered: Belgian Grand Prix preview: F1 returns to Spa with the title fight tightening

content.raw:
Formula 1 returns to the Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps for the Belgian Grand Prix on Sunday 19 July, the next round on the 2026 calendar. It follows a British Grand Prix that narrowed the championship and swung momentum toward Kimi Antonelli's rivals.

The title picture heading to Spa

Antonelli still leads the drivers' standings on 179 points, but his advantage over Mercedes team-mate George Russell fell to 25 points after Silverstone, according to the post-race standings. The gap closed because Antonelli scored no points in Britain, where a wheel-shield failure and a track-limits penalty dropped him out of the top ten, while Russell finished second.

Ferrari arrive with renewed form. Charles Leclerc won at Silverstone, his first victory of 2026, and Lewis Hamilton completed the podium in third. Mercedes still lead the constructors' standings on 333 points, 78 clear of Ferrari, though Leclerc's win closed the gap and gave the team its second Grand Prix victory of the year.

What makes Spa demanding

Spa-Francorchamps is the longest circuit on the calendar at 7.004 km, and the Grand Prix runs over just 44 laps — fewer than any other race of the season — for a distance of about 308 km. The lap climbs and falls through the Ardennes forest, most famously at the Eau Rouge and Raidillon complex, before the long Kemmel Straight opens the main overtaking zone. It is one of the fastest tracks of the year, and low-downforce running rewards cars that are efficient in a straight line.

Weather is the circuit's defining variable. The course is long enough that one sector can be dry while another is wet, and any setup is a compromise between straight-line speed and downforce through the middle sector. Few venues punish the wrong call more heavily, and rain has frequently shaped the outcome here.

What to watch

Antonelli's response is the central question. The 19-year-old has led most of the season with five wins and five poles, and Spa offers a chance to steady his campaign after his second pointless weekend of the season. Russell, a winner in Austria before Silverstone, will aim to keep closing the gap to his team-mate.

Ferrari's trajectory is the other storyline. Leclerc rediscovered the balance he had lacked in the SF-26 at Silverstone, and a strong result at Spa would confirm the recovery. Hamilton, a multiple past winner at the circuit, adds a third contender to a fight that has tightened over the past two rounds. A 25-point lead can narrow quickly at a circuit where weather and reliability weigh so heavily, and the result at Spa will help set the tone for the second half of the season.

Practice runs across Friday and Saturday, with qualifying on Saturday and the race scheduled for 15:00 local time on Sunday.

title.raw: Marquez owns the Sachsenring again as Martin keeps the title lead into the break
title.rendered: Marquez owns the Sachsenring again as Martin keeps the title lead into the break

content.raw:
The Sachsenring belongs to Marc Márquez, and 2026 was no different. The reigning champion took pole, set a new outright lap record, then led every lap of Saturday's Sprint and all 30 of Sunday's Grand Prix for a faultless weekend at the circuit he has ruled for over a decade. It was his tenth premier-class win at the Sachsenring, drawing him level with the great Giacomo Agostini. And yet he still leaves Germany only third in the championship.

The SachsenKing, untouchable again

The Italian press long ago nicknamed him the "SachsenKing", and the German Grand Prix was another clean sweep. Márquez won the Sprint by 0.368s and the Grand Prix by 1.996s, never headed in either, having opened the weekend with a record-breaking pole lap. It capped the run that has reshaped the title race: after the Italian Grand Prix at Mugello he trailed the championship leader by 102 points, and at the season's halfway mark that gap is down to 18. You can read how the win reshuffled the order on the MotoGP standings tab.

The rivals who threw it away

Márquez's closest Saturday challengers were both gone by Sunday afternoon. Álex Márquez, second in the Sprint, was running second again in the Grand Prix when he slid off at the final corner on lap 10. Fabio Di Giannantonio, third in the Sprint, crashed out of fifth in the early laps after already falling in warm-up. Two podium threats erased in a single afternoon, and the race behind Márquez broke wide open.

Trackhouse steps up

Into that gap rode Trackhouse Aprilia. Ai Ogura and Raúl Fernández ran home second and third for a Trackhouse one-two behind the winner, and they settled it between themselves on track: Ogura swept past his team-mate with six laps to run and pulled clear to take the runner-up spot. It is a big result for Ogura, who leaves Germany a clear second in the world championship and the closest man of all to the leader.

Martin holds the line

Jorge Martín never looked like winning, but leaders bank points on their quiet days, and he did exactly that. He held off Francesco Bagnaia to the flag for fifth, crossing the line 0.123s ahead of the Ducati to protect his advantage. Fortune helped him too: Marco Bezzecchi, second in the standings coming in, broke his collarbone in a qualifying crash and sat out the whole weekend, dropping to fourth as Márquez and Ogura leapfrogged him.

Top ten: 1. Márquez (Ducati Lenovo), 2. Ogura (Trackhouse Aprilia), 3. Raúl Fernández (Trackhouse Aprilia), 4. Acosta (Red Bull KTM), 5. Martín (Aprilia Racing), 6. Bagnaia (Ducati Lenovo), 7. Quartararo (Monster Yamaha), 8. Marini (Honda HRC), 9. Bastianini (Red Bull KTM Tech3), 10. Binder (Red Bull KTM). The full classification is on the results tab.

Where it leaves us

MotoGP heads into the summer break with its title fight squeezed into almost nothing: just 24 points cover the top five. Martín leads on 208, from Ogura on 194 (14 back), Márquez on 190 (18 back) and Bezzecchi on 186, with Di Giannantonio fifth on 184. The session-by-session weekend, results and reports are on the German Grand Prix page.

Márquez has the momentum, Martín has the lead, Ogura has the surprise, and all three get a month to sit with it. The season resumes at the British Grand Prix at Silverstone on 7-9 August, and none of them can afford to enjoy the break for long.

title.raw: F1 Belgian Grand Prix: Ferrari giving fans their dose of hopium, Antonelli's return to dominance: Belgium's Spa never disappoints
title.rendered: F1 Belgian Grand Prix: Ferrari giving fans their dose of hopium, Antonelli’s return to dominance: Belgium’s Spa never disappoints

content.raw:
Surviving the Belgian Grand Prix: not what Lewis Hamilton aimed for on Sunday morning. Somehow, as Ferrari always do, Hamilton managed to: crash into ex-teammate George Russell on the opening lap, serve a 5 second penalty in a 10.6 second pit stop, run over a mechanic, and finish fourth. The mechanic was unhurt, Ferrari swallowed a fine for the unsafe release, and the whole thing still ended in points. A usual Ferrari disaster-class converted into a 4th place.

Toto's unreliable rocketship

It would be a shame not to talk about Kimi Antonelli's ruthless competitiveness, paired with yet another of Toto's rocketships, which run circles around the entire grid when they don't decide to break down or have reliability issues. Pole on Saturday, his sixth of the year. Win on Sunday, also his sixth of the year. That is not a hot streak. That is a habit.

The rich stay rich

The new regulations punish some, award others. Cadillac and Aston Martin suffered a mechanical DNF apiece, as they have become accustomed to doing: suspension for Sergio Pérez on lap 13, gearbox for Lance Stroll on lap 25. Mercedes, Ferrari, McLaren and Red Bull spent yet another race well ahead of those behind.

Kemmel theatre

For us the viewers, some outstanding overtakes and defences on the Kemmel Straight; most notable of the former being Franco Colapinto's Häkkinen-esque double overtake over his own teammate Pierre Gasly and rival Liam Lawson. The best thing an Argentine did all Sunday. Charles Leclerc held the, in his own words, "too close for comfort" defence over Oscar Piastri, sharing a little contact going into Les Combes; Piastri's floor paid the price.

Russell breaks, Verstappen returns

Frankly, an entertaining race, and no complaints to be had for anyone other than George Russell, who faced yet another reliability issue: no power and no battery charge leaving La Source on lap 1. He called it dangerous; Toto Wolff called it "100 per cent on us". Neither was wrong. In contrast to the Brit's devastating result, the Dutchman Max Verstappen returned to the podium's third step now that his "Macarena" wing is gone and his beloved high-downforce-on-a-high-speed-track setup is back.

He had to win it twice

Leclerc and Antonelli proved they were in their own stratosphere, though we must note that Leclerc did win out with a well timed pit stop under the virtual safety car on lap 21, and for a dozen laps dared to pretend he had a chance at winning as he did in Britain's Silverstone. Then Antonelli hunted Leclerc's Ferrari down, re-passed him into Les Combes on lap 34, and cleared off: 1.952 seconds at the flag, six wins from ten, and a 45 point lead that is starting to read like a verdict.

Recovery school

As far as recovery drives go, Isack Hadjar and Lando Norris executed them beautifully. The French prodigy punished all the underdeveloped midfield and tractor teams, coming from the back of the grid to land himself a respectable points haul in sixth. And McLaren, fortunately, failed at sabotaging the reigning world champion with a 7.8 second pit stop (a left-rear that refused to leave), as Norris's consistent overdrive placed him seventh at the chequered flag. He reckons the stop and the safety-car timing cost him 16 seconds and a podium. McLaren, painfully, agree.

Two-time champion rookie Fernando Alonso spent yet another race watching the fast boys fly by, blue flags dominating his afternoon on the way to 19th, last of the classified runners and two laps down. (At least Spain's national football team brought him some much needed happiness later that night.)

Where it leaves us

Top ten: 1. Antonelli (Mercedes), 2. Leclerc (Ferrari), 3. Verstappen (Red Bull), 4. Hamilton (Ferrari), 5. Piastri (McLaren), 6. Hadjar (Red Bull), 7. Norris (McLaren), 8. Bortoleto (Audi), 9. Lindblad (Racing Bulls), 10. Colapinto (Alpine). (Full classification.)

Antonelli leaves Belgium on 204 points. Hamilton's recovery to fourth makes him the closest challenger on 159, 45 behind, with Russell third on 154 and now 50 adrift of the teammate he is supposed to be racing. Leclerc (126) and Norris (103) complete the top five. Formula 1 goes again next weekend at the Hungarian Grand Prix in Budapest, and after that the grid gets a month to lick its wounds.

title.raw: Belgian Grand Prix 2026, lap by lap: the Spa race in order
title.rendered: Belgian Grand Prix 2026, lap by lap: the Spa race in order

content.raw:
The result was Kimi Antonelli from Charles Leclerc and Max Verstappen, under two seconds covering the lead pair. The route there ran through two safety-car phases, two virtual ones, three retirements, four lead changes and a recovery drive from the back to sixth. In order:

Lap 1

Verstappen tows past Antonelli into Raidillon; Antonelli repasses up the Kemmel Straight. Behind, the midfield is already scrapping: Franco Colapinto picks off Pierre Gasly and Gabriel Bortoleto, Liam Lawson takes Bortoleto too, and Lando Norris, starting 13th on a grid penalty, is already moving. George Russell loses energy out of La Source, tumbles through the order, and is collected by Lewis Hamilton at Turn 6. Out. Safety car.

Laps 1-4: safety car

Field neutralised while Russell's Mercedes is recovered. Hamilton takes a five-second penalty for the contact.

Laps 5-17: green, and a charge through the field

Racing resumes and Isack Hadjar, starting from the back, begins the drive of the day: Esteban Ocon, Valtteri Bottas and Sergio Pérez on lap 5, Lance Stroll on lap 6, Oliver Bearman on lap 10, Carlos Sainz on lap 11, Alexander Albon on lap 12, Nico Hülkenberg on lap 13, and Bortoleto for the top ten on lap 15. Colapinto and Norris trade eighth on lap 8. Pérez retires on lap 13 with suspension failure. Up front, Antonelli still leads Leclerc.

Laps 18-23: the virtual safety car swing

  • L18-21: two VSC periods. Ferrari times its stop to perfection.
  • L19: Leclerc emerges ahead of Antonelli. New leader. Behind, Lawson and Gasly start a fight that runs for a dozen laps, swapping places on laps 19 and 21.
  • L21: Norris, offset on strategy, leads.
  • L23: Leclerc repasses Norris and pulls clear, three seconds in hand.

Laps 24-33: Leclerc controls

Leclerc leads in clean air; Antonelli, on the harder tyre, reels him in. Stroll retires on lap 25, gearbox. Sainz clears Ocon for 16th on lap 24. Colapinto lights up the midfield, taking Hülkenberg on lap 28 and a Häkkinen-style double into Les Combes on lap 29, then Lawson on lap 30. Lawson and Gasly are still at it, swapping again on laps 30 and 33.

Lap 34: the winning move

Antonelli takes the lead back from Leclerc at Les Combes. Clean, no contact. It is the last lead change of the race.

Laps 35-44: managed home

Antonelli controls the gap to the flag, under two seconds. Hamilton passes Oscar Piastri late for fourth, despite his penalty and an unsafe-release investigation.

Pit log (28 stops)

A one-stop race for most. Antonelli: medium to lap 18, hard to the end. Norris: 13th on the grid from a power-unit penalty, then a 7.8-second stop, recovered to seventh. Hadjar: from the back of the grid to sixth.

Retirements

  • L1 Russell (Mercedes), lap-one contact after an energy failure.
  • L13 Pérez (Cadillac), suspension.
  • L25 Stroll (Aston Martin), gearbox.

Where it leaves the title

Antonelli 204, Hamilton 159 (+45), Russell 154 (+50). Full classification and the weekend page. Next: the Hungarian Grand Prix.

Lap-by-lap movements are from OpenF1 timing; overtake coverage is not exhaustive.

Lap 1

Verstappen tows past Antonelli into Raidillon; Antonelli repasses up the Kemmel Straight. Behind, the midfield is already scrapping: Franco Colapinto picks off Pierre Gasly and Gabriel Bortoleto, Liam Lawson takes Bortoleto too, and Lando Norris, starting 13th on a grid penalty, is already moving. George Russell loses energy out of La Source, tumbles through the order, and is collected by Lewis Hamilton at Turn 6. Out. Safety car.

Laps 1-4: safety car

Field neutralised while Russell’s Mercedes is recovered. Hamilton takes a five-second penalty for the contact.

Laps 5-17: green, and a charge through the field

Racing resumes and Isack Hadjar, starting from the back, begins the drive of the day: Esteban Ocon, Valtteri Bottas and Sergio Pérez on lap 5, Lance Stroll on lap 6, Oliver Bearman on lap 10, Carlos Sainz on lap 11, Alexander Albon on lap 12, Nico Hülkenberg on lap 13, and Bortoleto for the top ten on lap 15. Colapinto and Norris trade eighth on lap 8. Pérez retires on lap 13 with suspension failure. Up front, Antonelli still leads Leclerc.

Laps 18-23: the virtual safety car swing

  • L18-21: two VSC periods. Ferrari times its stop to perfection.
  • L19: Leclerc emerges ahead of Antonelli. New leader. Behind, Lawson and Gasly start a fight that runs for a dozen laps, swapping places on laps 19 and 21.
  • L21: Norris, offset on strategy, leads.
  • L23: Leclerc repasses Norris and pulls clear, three seconds in hand.

Laps 24-33: Leclerc controls

Leclerc leads in clean air; Antonelli, on the harder tyre, reels him in. Stroll retires on lap 25, gearbox. Sainz clears Ocon for 16th on lap 24. Colapinto lights up the midfield, taking Hülkenberg on lap 28 and a Häkkinen-style double into Les Combes on lap 29, then Lawson on lap 30. Lawson and Gasly are still at it, swapping again on laps 30 and 33.

Lap 34: the winning move

Antonelli takes the lead back from Leclerc at Les Combes. Clean, no contact. It is the last lead change of the race.

Laps 35-44: managed home

Antonelli controls the gap to the flag, under two seconds. Hamilton passes Oscar Piastri late for fourth, despite his penalty and an unsafe-release investigation.

Pit log (28 stops)

A one-stop race for most. Antonelli: medium to lap 18, hard to the end. Norris: 13th on the grid from a power-unit penalty, then a 7.8-second stop, recovered to seventh. Hadjar: from the back of the grid to sixth.

Retirements

  • L1 Russell (Mercedes), lap-one contact after an energy failure.
  • L13 Pérez (Cadillac), suspension.
  • L25 Stroll (Aston Martin), gearbox.

Where it leaves the title

Antonelli 204, Hamilton 159 (+45), Russell 154 (+50). Full classification and the weekend page. Next: the Hungarian Grand Prix.

Lap-by-lap movements are from OpenF1 timing; overtake coverage is not exhaustive.

content.raw:
By Stylianos Christopoulos

«Δεν μπορεί, γιατί δεν έχει την εμπειρία του Russell». «Μην χαίρεστε ακόμα, γιατί και πέρυσι δυσκολεύτηκε όταν ξεκίνησε το ευρωπαϊκό stint». Αυτά και πολλά άλλα ειπώθηκαν κατά τη διάρκεια της φετινής σεζόν για τον Kimi Antonelli, ωστόσο ο πιτσιρικάς έχει βαλθεί να μας τρελάνει.

Πρώτη νίκη στο Grand Prix του Βελγίου για τον 19χρονο Ιταλό, ο οποίος μάλιστα είδε τον συμπαίκτη του και championship rival George Russell να έχει επαφή με τον Hamilton και να εγκαταλείπει στο πρώτο lap του αγώνα. Πέρα από αυτό το γεγονός όμως, Norris και Hadjar έδειξαν τα δόντια τους με την εκπληκτική οδήγησή τους, ενώ είχαμε εξαιρετικές μάχες και στο midfield με τις Racing Bulls και Alpine, οι οποίες έδειξαν πάλι πως είναι υπολογίσιμες δυνάμεις για το μέλλον. Εν τέλει, τι θετικά και τι αρνητικά κρατάει κάθε ομάδα από αυτό το σαββατοκύριακο;

Mercedes

Θετικά: Τα Silver Arrows είδαν σοβαρή πρόοδο με την αναβάθμιση στο πάτωμα, η οποία τους έδωσε το πάνω χέρι στα sector 1 και 3, ισορροπώντας το μέτριο sector 2 και την αδυναμία στα low speed corners. Φυσικά υπάρχει ικανοποίηση και για την έκτη φετινή νίκη του «μικρού» Antonelli, ο οποίος δεν έδειξε να επηρεάζεται και κατάφερε με ένα πανέμορφο ERS management να ξεπεράσει τον Leclerc στην Kemmel. Επιπλέον, έγινε σωστή χρήση στρατηγικής και ηρεμίας από τη Mercedes, η οποία δεν πανικοβλήθηκε μετά το VSC, δίνοντας εντολή στον Antonelli να «ζεστάνει» τα ελαστικά στο dirty air του Leclerc προτού βρεθεί η «χρυσή» ευκαιρία επίθεσης.

Αρνητικά: Δυστυχώς, η παράπλευρη απώλεια σε ένα κατά τα άλλα τέλειο σαββατοκύριακο ήταν η διαχείριση του Russell. Όπως φάνηκε και από τα practice, υπήρχε δυσκολία σε πολλούς τομείς τόσο για τον ίδιο όσο και για την ομάδα, με κύριο πρόβλημα την τελική επιτάχυνση στην ευθεία, κάτι που επιβεβαιώθηκε και στο race start. Η σύγκρουση με τον Hamilton ήταν η σταγόνα που ξεχείλισε το ποτήρι, με τον ίδιο να δηλώνει εμφανώς δυσαρεστημένος με το SoC της μπαταρίας (δείχνει πόση ενέργεια είναι αποθηκευμένη στην μπαταρία του υβριδικού συστήματος) και την έλλειψή της μετά την Eau Rouge, κάτι που οδήγησε σε πιο επιθετική οδήγηση και εν τέλει στην εγκατάλειψη.

Ferrari

Θετικά: Άλλο ένα ΣΚ στο οποίο ο Leclerc δείχνει τα δόντια του και καταφέρνει να πάρει πολύτιμους βαθμούς για τη Scuderia και το constructors. Εξαιρετική απόδοση και από τον ομόσταυλό του, τον Hamilton, ο οποίος παρά το penalty κατάφερε να σκαρφαλώσει μέχρι και την τέταρτη θέση. Η απόφαση της ομάδας να φωνάξει και τους δύο στα pits στο δευτερόλεπτο που ενεργοποιήθηκε το εικονικό αυτοκίνητο ασφαλείας τούς γλίτωσε περίπου δέκα δευτερόλεπτα σε σχέση με ένα pit stop υπό κανονικές συνθήκες και εξισορρόπησε τις όποιες «αναποδιές» είχαν προκληθεί στην αρχή. Επίσης, η SF-26 έδειξε ότι έχει λύσει το πρόβλημα των αναπηδήσεων (bouncing) στις γρήγορες στροφές, καθιστώντας τη μια μεγαλύτερη απειλή στη μάχη με τη Mercedes.

Αρνητικά: Είναι πλέον εμφανής η δυσκολία της Ferrari να κρατήσει το pace της με τη σκληρή γόμα, γεγονός που αποδείχτηκε και σήμερα το μελανό σημείο, καθώς ο Leclerc (όταν τον έφτασε ο Antonelli) αποδείχτηκε εύκολη λεία. Πέρα από αυτό, είδαμε το κακό gamble της Ferrari να θυσιάσει τη straight line speed για να κερδίσει ακόμη περισσότερο στο sector 2 (όντας το αδύναμο σημείο της Mercedes), κάτι που κόστισε στο τέλος και στο comeback του Hamilton. Μιας και μιλάμε για τον κύριο Hamilton, θα πρέπει να αναφερθούμε και στο unsafe release του στα pits, όπου παρέσυρε έναν μηχανικό (ο οποίος ευτυχώς αποδείχτηκε πως ήταν καλά μετά τη σύγκρουση), δείχνοντας για ακόμη μια φορά τα λάθη του pit crew υπό πίεση. Να σημειωθεί πως επιβλήθηκε και πρόστιμο 30.000 ευρώ στη Scuderia για αυτό το γεγονός.

McLaren

Θετικά: Δαιμονιώδης ο ρυθμός του Lando Norris, ο οποίος δεν φάνηκε επηρεασμένος από την ποινή 10 θέσεων λόγω αλλαγής στοιχείων της μονάδας ισχύος και με μια φανταστική επίδειξη οδήγησης κατάφερε να φτάσει μέχρι την 7η θέση. Ειδικά στο τελευταίο stint με τη μεσαία γόμα ήταν με διαφορά ο πιο γρήγορος άνθρωπος στην πίστα, σημειώνοντας 13 σερί ταχύτερους γύρους και μειώνοντας τη διαφορά από τους προπορευόμενους κατά 0.7 με 1 δευτερόλεπτο τον γύρο (ναι, σωστά το διαβάσατε). Σε παρόμοιους ρυθμούς κινήθηκε και ο συμπαίκτης του Oscar Piastri, ο οποίος τερμάτισε στην 5η θέση δίνοντας αρκετές μάχες, παρά τη ζημιά που υπέστη το πάτωμα του μονοθεσίου του, και κρατώντας ζωντανή τη μεσαία γόμα μέχρι το lap 20, επιτρέποντας έτσι τη στρατηγική του one stop.

Αρνητικά: Δυστυχώς για τον Lando, παρά τον εκπληκτικό αγώνα του, οι ελπίδες του ακόμη και για podium έσβησαν με το αργό pit stop των 7.8 δευτερολέπτων (πρόβλημα στον πίσω αριστερό τροχό) και με τους γύρους που έμεινε κολλημένος πίσω από την Audi του Bortoleto μέχρι να βρει τρόπο να περάσει. Η επιλογή του high downforce, παρότι του έδινε από τα καλύτερα sector 2 (αν όχι το καλύτερο), δυσκόλευε σημαντικά κάθε προσπέραση στην ευθεία μετά την Eau Rouge.

Red Bull

Θετικά: Τι να πούμε για αυτόν τον Hadjar! Ξεκινώντας 21ος, έβαλε τη σκληρή γόμα και τράβηξε το πρώτο του stint πιο μακριά από όλο το midfield γύρω του, πράγμα που φάνηκε δύσκολο μετά το γρήγορο VSC· ωστόσο, εκμεταλλευόμενος το clean air όταν οι υπόλοιποι μπήκαν στα pits, πραγματοποίησε τη μία προσπέραση μετά την άλλη, κερδίζοντας 15 θέσεις μέχρι την 6η θέση στον τερματισμό. Βέβαια, δεν θα πρέπει να ξεχνάμε και την πολύ καλή οδήγηση του Max Verstappen, ο οποίος μάλιστα έκανε μια μαγευτική κίνηση (αν και εν τέλει δεν απέδωσε καρπούς) στην Eau Rouge, βρισκόμενος για λίγο στην 1η θέση πριν προσπεραστεί ξανά από τον Kimi. Αυτή η υψηλού ρίσκου κίνηση τού έδωσε τη δυνατότητα να «ελέγξει» καλύτερα τον ανταγωνισμό και να φτάσει μέχρι το podium στο τέλος.

Αρνητικά: Όπως ακούστηκε και στα team radio, ο Verstappen πάλεψε σε όλο τον αγώνα με κρύα μπροστινά ελαστικά και έλλειψη πρόσφυσης με τη σκληρή γόμα («no front bite»), κάτι που δεν του επέτρεψε να απειλήσει πραγματικά το δίδυμο της κορυφής.

Audi

Θετικά: Η Audi έχει πραγματοποιήσει άλματα προόδου από την αρχή της σεζόν και αυτό φαίνεται. Εξαιρετικός ο Bortoleto στην 8η θέση, με ένα αμάξι που έδειξε αρκετή σταθερότητα. Μεγάλα εύσημα πρέπει να λάβει και η ομάδα για τη σωστή επιλογή και το σωστό timing να «τραβήξει» και τους δύο οδηγούς μέσα στα pits για αλλαγή ελαστικών κάτω από το VSC, μια κίνηση που πέταξε τον Bortoleto μπροστά από τις Racing Bulls.

Αρνητικά: Δυστυχώς, ο Hülkenberg είναι σκιά του εαυτού του. Άλλο ένα Σαββατοκύριακο, άλλη μια απογοήτευση για τον midfield king, η οποία κορυφώθηκε όταν το αμάξι του παρουσίασε πρόβλημα μέχρι και στο qualifying, και συγκεκριμένα στο τέλος του Q2. Όπως είπε και ο ίδιος, δυστυχώς έμεινε θεατής στη μάχη των Gasly, Colapinto και Lawson και δεν μπόρεσε να διεκδικήσει κάτι παραπάνω. Θα πρέπει να ακολουθήσει τον ρυθμό του Bortoleto αν θέλει η Audi να έχει βλέψεις για κάτι παραπάνω στην κατάταξη των κατασκευαστών.

Alpine

Θετικά: Αν κάποιος έπρεπε να κρατήσει ένα highlight από το weekend, αυτό θα ήταν σίγουρα η απίστευτη διπλή προσπέραση του Colapinto σε Gasly και Lawson. Ο Αργεντινός συνεχίζει τις εκπληκτικές εμφανίσεις, μπαίνοντας στους πόντους στα 6 από τα 10 φετινά Grand Prix και συμβάλλοντας τα μέγιστα στη μάχη της 5ης θέσης των κατασκευαστών.

Αρνητικά: Η Alpine στέρησε από τον Gasly μια πιθανή θέση στους πόντους με ένα αργό pit stop που τον έριξε πίσω στην κίνηση: ο Γάλλος έμεινε κολλημένος εκεί για πολλούς γύρους και τερμάτισε 11ος, μόλις μία θέση έξω από τη βαθμολογούμενη δεκάδα.

Racing Bulls

Θετικά: Για ακόμα ένα Grand Prix, ο Arvid Lindblad συνεχίζει τις σταθερές επιδόσεις του. Άλλη μια είσοδος στο Q3 και 9η θέση για τον πιτσιρικά, ο οποίος συνεχίζει να εκπλήσσει και θέτει τα θεμέλια για κάτι μεγαλύτερο (ίσως να κερδίσει και τη θέση σε μια από τις μεγάλες ομάδες).

Αρνητικά: Το εσωτερικό ντέρμπι των δύο οδηγών ξέφυγε: αγγίχτηκαν ρόδα με ρόδα στο πρώτο lap και ξαναβρέθηκαν δίπλα δίπλα στα μισά του αγώνα, με τον Lawson να βγαίνει δύο φορές εκτός πίστας στη Les Combes (η FIA το σημείωσε, χωρίς να ανοίξει έρευνα). Ο Lawson πάλεψε επιπλέον με προβλήματα στην αποδέσμευση ενέργειας σε όλο τον αγώνα, όπως επιβεβαίωσε και ο επικεφαλής της ομάδας, και εν τέλει έμεινε εκτός βαθμών, στη 12η θέση, πίσω και από τις δύο Alpine.

Haas

Θετικά: Τηρουμένων των αναλογιών, η Haas είχε μια σταθερή πορεία μέχρι τον τερματισμό, χωρίς τα μονοθέσια να παρουσιάσουν κάποιου είδους πρόβλημα από τεχνικής απόψεως.

Αρνητικά: Ο Ocon συνεχίζει το «ντεφορμάρισμα» και βλέπει τον Bearman να τον ξεπερνάει για ακόμη μια φορά (βέβαια, είχε και την επαφή με τον Sainz, στην οποία δεν έφταιγε και η οποία του στοίχισε κλατάρισμα και ένα έξτρα pit stop από το πρώτο κιόλας lap), ενώ ταυτόχρονα φαίνεται πως το μονοθέσιο έχει φτάσει το ταβάνι του, τουλάχιστον για τη φετινή χρονιά.

Williams

Θετικά: Σε ένα απαιτητικό weekend που δεν ξεκίνησε με τους καλύτερους οιωνούς, η Williams κατάφερε να οδηγήσει και τα δύο μονοθέσια στον τερματισμό, συλλέγοντας πληθώρα δεδομένων για τη συνέχεια.

Αρνητικά: Άλλο ένα σαββατοκύριακο όπου αμάξι της Williams έχει επαφή στο opening lap. Ο Sainz χτύπησε στο πίσω μέρος του Ocon στην πρώτη στροφή, καταστρέφοντας το εμπρός φτερό του και το πλάνο του αγώνα του (ήταν ένας από τους μόλις δύο οδηγούς, μαζί με τον Bottas, που ξεκίνησαν με τη μαλακή γόμα), ενώ γενικότερα παρουσιάστηκε μια αδυναμία των μονοθεσίων στις γρήγορες στροφές, η οποία κατέστρεφε τα ελαστικά τους.

Aston Martin

Θετικά: Αν κάποιος έψαχνε κάτι θετικό από αυτό το GP για την Aston, θα ήταν ίσως το γεγονός πως ο Alonso συνέλεξε δεδομένα σχετικά με το αεροδυναμικό πακέτο του μονοθεσίου.

Αρνητικά: Η Aston επέλεξε την αξιοπιστία πάνω από την απόδοση. Το αποτέλεσμα; Τελική ταχύτητα 249 χλμ./ώρα, η πιο αργή τελική στις μέρες μας, όχι μόνο για τα δεδομένα της F1 αλλά ακόμα και της F3! Νομίζουμε πως μόνο και μόνο το γεγονός ότι ο Alonso έκανε «κοιλιές» στο τέλος του αγώνα, τερματίζοντας 2 γύρους πίσω από τον νικητή, δείχνει τη λυπηρή κατάσταση που επικρατεί στο γκαράζ και στις τάξεις αυτής της ομάδας.

Cadillac

Θετικά: Η αλήθεια είναι πως με γυμνό μάτι δεν μπορεί να διακρίνει κάποιος τα θετικά. Ωστόσο, βλέποντας τα δεδομένα κάθε εβδομάδας, η Cadillac φαίνεται να βελτιώνεται μέρα με τη μέρα, σε σημείο να παλεύει με τη Haas και τη Williams για μια θέση στο Q2 (ναι, διαβάσατε σωστά). Επιπλέον, βλέπουμε και στον αγώνα πως τα μονοθέσια μπορεί να είναι ακόμα πίσω στο development, αλλά φτάνουν όλο και πιο κοντά στο να βρουν το «δικό» τους race pace.

Αρνητικά: Δυστυχώς, ο Pérez χρειάστηκε να εγκαταλείψει με μηχανική βλάβη για ακόμα μια φορά, δείχνοντας πως το κύριο πρόβλημα της ομάδας είναι η αξιοπιστία και η προσαρμογή στους νέους κανονισμούς.

Ο απολογισμός

Το φετινό, ανανεωμένο με τα καινούργια regulations Spa μάς αφήνει ένα race που τα είχε σχεδόν όλα. Σίγουρα κερδισμένοι είναι ο Kimi και η Ferrari γενικότερα, ενώ συναρπαστικά races είχαν οι Norris, Hadjar και Bortoleto, οι οποίοι συνέλεξαν πολύτιμους βαθμούς για τη συνέχεια. Η μεγάλη απογοήτευση του φετινού Grand Prix ήταν ο George Russell, ο οποίος είδε άλλο ένα «χαμένο» σαββατοκύριακο στην προσπάθειά του να μειώσει την απόσταση από την κορυφή, ενώ αδικημένοι θα πρέπει να νιώθουν οι Gasly και Lawson: του πρώτου το αργό pit stop και του δεύτερου τα προβλήματα ενέργειας και οι σκληρές μάχες τούς στέρησαν την ευκαιρία για κάτι καλύτερο. Σειρά τώρα έχει το Grand Prix της Ουγγαρίας και αναμένουμε και εκεί μεγάλη αγωνία και δράση μέχρι τέλους. Θα μπορέσουν να κλείσουν την ψαλίδα με την κορυφή οι Hamilton και Russell ή θα έχουμε άλλο ένα masterclass του Antonelli που θα τον φέρει πιο κοντά στον τίτλο;

Η σύγκρουση με τον Hamilton ήταν η σταγόνα που ξεχείλισε το ποτήρι, με τον ίδιο να δηλώνει εμφανώς δυσαρεστημένος με το SoC της μπαταρίας (δείχνει πόση ενέργεια είναι αποθηκευμένη στην μπαταρία του υβριδικού συστήματος) και την έλλειψή της μετά την Eau Rouge, κάτι που οδήγησε σε πιο επιθετική οδήγηση και εν τέλει στην εγκατάλειψη.

Ferrari

Θετικά: Άλλο ένα ΣΚ στο οποίο ο Leclerc δείχνει τα δόντια του και καταφέρνει να πάρει πολύτιμους βαθμούς για τη Scuderia και το constructors. Εξαιρετική απόδοση και από τον ομόσταυλό του, τον Hamilton, ο οποίος παρά το penalty κατάφερε να σκαρφαλώσει μέχρι και την τέταρτη θέση. Η απόφαση της ομάδας να φωνάξει και τους δύο στα pits στο δευτερόλεπτο που ενεργοποιήθηκε το εικονικό αυτοκίνητο ασφαλείας τούς γλίτωσε περίπου δέκα δευτερόλεπτα σε σχέση με ένα pit stop υπό κανονικές συνθήκες και εξισορρόπησε τις όποιες «αναποδιές» είχαν προκληθεί στην αρχή. Επίσης, η SF-26 έδειξε ότι έχει λύσει το πρόβλημα των αναπηδήσεων (bouncing) στις γρήγορες στροφές, καθιστώντας τη μια μεγαλύτερη απειλή στη μάχη με τη Mercedes.

Αρνητικά: Είναι πλέον εμφανής η δυσκολία της Ferrari να κρατήσει το pace της με τη σκληρή γόμα, γεγονός που αποδείχτηκε και σήμερα το μελανό σημείο, καθώς ο Leclerc (όταν τον έφτασε ο Antonelli) αποδείχτηκε εύκολη λεία. Πέρα από αυτό, είδαμε το κακό gamble της Ferrari να θυσιάσει τη straight line speed για να κερδίσει ακόμη περισσότερο στο sector 2 (όντας το αδύναμο σημείο της Mercedes), κάτι που κόστισε στο τέλος και στο comeback του Hamilton. Μιας και μιλάμε για τον κύριο Hamilton, θα πρέπει να αναφερθούμε και στο unsafe release του στα pits, όπου παρέσυρε έναν μηχανικό (ο οποίος ευτυχώς αποδείχτηκε πως ήταν καλά μετά τη σύγκρουση), δείχνοντας για ακόμη μια φορά τα λάθη του pit crew υπό πίεση. Να σημειωθεί πως επιβλήθηκε και πρόστιμο 30.000 ευρώ στη Scuderia για αυτό το γεγονός.

McLaren

Θετικά: Δαιμονιώδης ο ρυθμός του Lando Norris, ο οποίος δεν φάνηκε επηρεασμένος από την ποινή 10 θέσεων λόγω αλλαγής στοιχείων της μονάδας ισχύος και με μια φανταστική επίδειξη οδήγησης κατάφερε να φτάσει μέχρι την 7η θέση. Ειδικά στο τελευταίο stint με τη μεσαία γόμα ήταν με διαφορά ο πιο γρήγορος άνθρωπος στην πίστα, σημειώνοντας 13 σερί ταχύτερους γύρους και μειώνοντας τη διαφορά από τους προπορευόμενους κατά 0.7 με 1 δευτερόλεπτο τον γύρο (ναι, σωστά το διαβάσατε). Σε παρόμοιους ρυθμούς κινήθηκε και ο συμπαίκτης του Oscar Piastri, ο οποίος τερμάτισε στην 5η θέση δίνοντας αρκετές μάχες, παρά τη ζημιά που υπέστη το πάτωμα του μονοθεσίου του, και κρατώντας ζωντανή τη μεσαία γόμα μέχρι το lap 20, επιτρέποντας έτσι τη στρατηγική του one stop.

Αρνητικά: Δυστυχώς για τον Lando, παρά τον εκπληκτικό αγώνα του, οι ελπίδες του ακόμη και για podium έσβησαν με το αργό pit stop των 7.8 δευτερολέπτων (πρόβλημα στον πίσω αριστερό τροχό) και με τους γύρους που έμεινε κολλημένος πίσω από την Audi του Bortoleto μέχρι να βρει τρόπο να περάσει. Η επιλογή του high downforce, παρότι του έδινε από τα καλύτερα sector 2 (αν όχι το καλύτερο), δυσκόλευε σημαντικά κάθε προσπέραση στην ευθεία μετά την Eau Rouge.

Red Bull

Θετικά: Τι να πούμε για αυτόν τον Hadjar! Ξεκινώντας 21ος, έβαλε τη σκληρή γόμα και τράβηξε το πρώτο του stint πιο μακριά από όλο το midfield γύρω του, πράγμα που φάνηκε δύσκολο μετά το γρήγορο VSC· ωστόσο, εκμεταλλευόμενος το clean air όταν οι υπόλοιποι μπήκαν στα pits, πραγματοποίησε τη μία προσπέραση μετά την άλλη, κερδίζοντας 15 θέσεις μέχρι την 6η θέση στον τερματισμό. Βέβαια, δεν θα πρέπει να ξεχνάμε και την πολύ καλή οδήγηση του Max Verstappen, ο οποίος μάλιστα έκανε μια μαγευτική κίνηση (αν και εν τέλει δεν απέδωσε καρπούς) στην Eau Rouge, βρισκόμενος για λίγο στην 1η θέση πριν προσπεραστεί ξανά από τον Kimi. Αυτή η υψηλού ρίσκου κίνηση τού έδωσε τη δυνατότητα να «ελέγξει» καλύτερα τον ανταγωνισμό και να φτάσει μέχρι το podium στο τέλος.

Αρνητικά: Όπως ακούστηκε και στα team radio, ο Verstappen πάλεψε σε όλο τον αγώνα με κρύα μπροστινά ελαστικά και έλλειψη πρόσφυσης με τη σκληρή γόμα («no front bite»), κάτι που δεν του επέτρεψε να απειλήσει πραγματικά το δίδυμο της κορυφής.

Audi

Θετικά: Η Audi έχει πραγματοποιήσει άλματα προόδου από την αρχή της σεζόν και αυτό φαίνεται. Εξαιρετικός ο Bortoleto στην 8η θέση, με ένα αμάξι που έδειξε αρκετή σταθερότητα. Μεγάλα εύσημα πρέπει να λάβει και η ομάδα για τη σωστή επιλογή και το σωστό timing να «τραβήξει» και τους δύο οδηγούς μέσα στα pits για αλλαγή ελαστικών κάτω από το VSC, μια κίνηση που πέταξε τον Bortoleto μπροστά από τις Racing Bulls.

Αρνητικά: Δυστυχώς, ο Hülkenberg είναι σκιά του εαυτού του. Άλλο ένα Σαββατοκύριακο, άλλη μια απογοήτευση για τον midfield king, η οποία κορυφώθηκε όταν το αμάξι του παρουσίασε πρόβλημα μέχρι και στο qualifying, και συγκεκριμένα στο τέλος του Q2. Όπως είπε και ο ίδιος, δυστυχώς έμεινε θεατής στη μάχη των Gasly, Colapinto και Lawson και δεν μπόρεσε να διεκδικήσει κάτι παραπάνω. Θα πρέπει να ακολουθήσει τον ρυθμό του Bortoleto αν θέλει η Audi να έχει βλέψεις για κάτι παραπάνω στην κατάταξη των κατασκευαστών.

Alpine

Θετικά: Αν κάποιος έπρεπε να κρατήσει ένα highlight από το weekend, αυτό θα ήταν σίγουρα η απίστευτη διπλή προσπέραση του Colapinto σε Gasly και Lawson. Ο Αργεντινός συνεχίζει τις εκπληκτικές εμφανίσεις, μπαίνοντας στους πόντους στα 6 από τα 10 φετινά Grand Prix και συμβάλλοντας τα μέγιστα στη μάχη της 5ης θέσης των κατασκευαστών.

Αρνητικά: Η Alpine στέρησε από τον Gasly μια πιθανή θέση στους πόντους με ένα αργό pit stop που τον έριξε πίσω στην κίνηση: ο Γάλλος έμεινε κολλημένος εκεί για πολλούς γύρους και τερμάτισε 11ος, μόλις μία θέση έξω από τη βαθμολογούμενη δεκάδα.

Racing Bulls

Θετικά: Για ακόμα ένα Grand Prix, ο Arvid Lindblad συνεχίζει τις σταθερές επιδόσεις του. Άλλη μια είσοδος στο Q3 και 9η θέση για τον πιτσιρικά, ο οποίος συνεχίζει να εκπλήσσει και θέτει τα θεμέλια για κάτι μεγαλύτερο (ίσως να κερδίσει και τη θέση σε μια από τις μεγάλες ομάδες).

Αρνητικά: Το εσωτερικό ντέρμπι των δύο οδηγών ξέφυγε: αγγίχτηκαν ρόδα με ρόδα στο πρώτο lap και ξαναβρέθηκαν δίπλα δίπλα στα μισά του αγώνα, με τον Lawson να βγαίνει δύο φορές εκτός πίστας στη Les Combes (η FIA το σημείωσε, χωρίς να ανοίξει έρευνα). Ο Lawson πάλεψε επιπλέον με προβλήματα στην αποδέσμευση ενέργειας σε όλο τον αγώνα, όπως επιβεβαίωσε και ο επικεφαλής της ομάδας, και εν τέλει έμεινε εκτός βαθμών, στη 12η θέση, πίσω και από τις δύο Alpine.

Haas

Θετικά: Τηρουμένων των αναλογιών, η Haas είχε μια σταθερή πορεία μέχρι τον τερματισμό, χωρίς τα μονοθέσια να παρουσιάσουν κάποιου είδους πρόβλημα από τεχνικής απόψεως.

Αρνητικά: Ο Ocon συνεχίζει το «ντεφορμάρισμα» και βλέπει τον Bearman να τον ξεπερνάει για ακόμη μια φορά (βέβαια, είχε και την επαφή με τον Sainz, στην οποία δεν έφταιγε και η οποία του στοίχισε κλατάρισμα και ένα έξτρα pit stop από το πρώτο κιόλας lap), ενώ ταυτόχρονα φαίνεται πως το μονοθέσιο έχει φτάσει το ταβάνι του, τουλάχιστον για τη φετινή χρονιά.

Williams

Θετικά: Σε ένα απαιτητικό weekend που δεν ξεκίνησε με τους καλύτερους οιωνούς, η Williams κατάφερε να οδηγήσει και τα δύο μονοθέσια στον τερματισμό, συλλέγοντας πληθώρα δεδομένων για τη συνέχεια.

Αρνητικά: Άλλο ένα σαββατοκύριακο όπου αμάξι της Williams έχει επαφή στο opening lap. Ο Sainz χτύπησε στο πίσω μέρος του Ocon στην πρώτη στροφή, καταστρέφοντας το εμπρός φτερό του και το πλάνο του αγώνα του (ήταν ένας από τους μόλις δύο οδηγούς, μαζί με τον Bottas, που ξεκίνησαν με τη μαλακή γόμα), ενώ γενικότερα παρουσιάστηκε μια αδυναμία των μονοθεσίων στις γρήγορες στροφές, η οποία κατέστρεφε τα ελαστικά τους.

Aston Martin

Θετικά: Αν κάποιος έψαχνε κάτι θετικό από αυτό το GP για την Aston, θα ήταν ίσως το γεγονός πως ο Alonso συνέλεξε δεδομένα σχετικά με το αεροδυναμικό πακέτο του μονοθεσίου.

Αρνητικά: Η Aston επέλεξε την αξιοπιστία πάνω από την απόδοση. Το αποτέλεσμα; Τελική ταχύτητα 249 χλμ./ώρα, η πιο αργή τελική στις μέρες μας, όχι μόνο για τα δεδομένα της F1 αλλά ακόμα και της F3! Νομίζουμε πως μόνο και μόνο το γεγονός ότι ο Alonso έκανε «κοιλιές» στο τέλος του αγώνα, τερματίζοντας 2 γύρους πίσω από τον νικητή, δείχνει τη λυπηρή κατάσταση που επικρατεί στο γκαράζ και στις τάξεις αυτής της ομάδας.

Cadillac

Θετικά: Η αλήθεια είναι πως με γυμνό μάτι δεν μπορεί να διακρίνει κάποιος τα θετικά. Ωστόσο, βλέποντας τα δεδομένα κάθε εβδομάδας, η Cadillac φαίνεται να βελτιώνεται μέρα με τη μέρα, σε σημείο να παλεύει με τη Haas και τη Williams για μια θέση στο Q2 (ναι, διαβάσατε σωστά). Επιπλέον, βλέπουμε και στον αγώνα πως τα μονοθέσια μπορεί να είναι ακόμα πίσω στο development, αλλά φτάνουν όλο και πιο κοντά στο να βρουν το «δικό» τους race pace.

Αρνητικά: Δυστυχώς, ο Pérez χρειάστηκε να εγκαταλείψει με μηχανική βλάβη για ακόμα μια φορά, δείχνοντας πως το κύριο πρόβλημα της ομάδας είναι η αξιοπιστία και η προσαρμογή στους νέους κανονισμούς.

Ο απολογισμός

Το φετινό, ανανεωμένο με τα καινούργια regulations Spa μάς αφήνει ένα race που τα είχε σχεδόν όλα. Σίγουρα κερδισμένοι είναι ο Kimi και η Ferrari γενικότερα, ενώ συναρπαστικά races είχαν οι Norris, Hadjar και Bortoleto, οι οποίοι συνέλεξαν πολύτιμους βαθμούς για τη συνέχεια. Η μεγάλη απογοήτευση του φετινού Grand Prix ήταν ο George Russell, ο οποίος είδε άλλο ένα «χαμένο» σαββατοκύριακο στην προσπάθειά του να μειώσει την απόσταση από την κορυφή, ενώ αδικημένοι θα πρέπει να νιώθουν οι Gasly και Lawson: του πρώτου το αργό pit stop και του δεύτερου τα προβλήματα ενέργειας και οι σκληρές μάχες τούς στέρησαν την ευκαιρία για κάτι καλύτερο. Σειρά τώρα έχει το Grand Prix της Ουγγαρίας και αναμένουμε και εκεί μεγάλη αγωνία και δράση μέχρι τέλους. Θα μπορέσουν να κλείσουν την ψαλίδα με την κορυφή οι Hamilton και Russell ή θα έχουμε άλλο ένα masterclass του Antonelli που θα τον φέρει πιο κοντά στον τίτλο;

title.raw: Hungarian GP Preview: Ferrari fancy it, Hamilton owns it, Antonelli leads it: welcome to Monaco without the walls
title.rendered: Hungarian GP Preview: Ferrari fancy it, Hamilton owns it, Antonelli leads it: welcome to Monaco without the walls

content.raw:
The Hungarian Grand Prix is the eleventh of twenty-two rounds, which makes Sunday the exact halfway point of the season and the last thing anyone does before disappearing for three weeks. Kimi Antonelli turns up 45 points clear, six wins from ten, and the youngest championship leader the sport has ever had. He would quite like to spend August sitting on a lead that reads like a verdict. The Hungaroring, inconveniently for him, is the one track on the calendar built to make a Mercedes look ordinary and a Ferrari look reborn.

Half-term report

Antonelli leads on 204, and the genuinely interesting fight is the one behind him. Three drivers are squabbling over second: Lewis Hamilton on 159, George Russell on 154 and Charles Leclerc on 126, covered by 33 points, two of whom spent the first lap of Belgium trading paint and blame before Hamilton collected a penalty and Russell collected a gravel trap. The standings describe a title race that is really a procession with an excellent undercard.

Monaco without the walls

They call the Hungaroring "Monaco without the walls", and they are not being generous. Fourteen corners, one actual straight, and overtaking that has always run from difficult to strictly theoretical. Whether that survives 2026 is the open question: this is the first time the new cars, with their active aero and an override boost where DRS used to be, have seen the place, and nobody yet knows whether they crack it open or leave it as sealed as ever. Good. Keep everyone guessing. The rest has not changed: a high-downforce, low-patience track where the corners spill into one another and a single mistake ruins the next three, where keeping the brakes cool is harder than stopping the car, and where Saturday afternoon probably still decides Sunday. A one-stop usually wins. Track position is usually everything, though "usually" is carrying more weight this year than it used to. It is also where Esteban Ocon won his only race in 2021, purely because everyone ahead of him crashed, so the place is not above the occasional act of God.

Ferrari's to fancy

Which brings us to Ferrari and the annual delivery of hopium. The SF-26 has spent the year a few kph shy of Toto's rocketships in a straight line, but it has been one of the best cars in the sport through the corners, and the Hungaroring offers precisely nowhere to hide the difference. They have reportedly bolted even more downforce onto it for the occasion. Leclerc has taken pole here in each of the last two years and won on neither, which is either a warning or a tradition. Hamilton has won at this circuit a record eight times and treats it like a second home, a claim only slightly undermined by his twelfth place here last summer. If Ferrari cannot win this weekend, they should probably stop promising that they can.

The corner myth

None of which means Antonelli is in any bother, and here is the bit the Ferrari optimists would rather skip. On a track with no straights, Mercedes' one flaw, straight-line speed, stops mattering at all. But the real tell came in Belgium's second sector, the twisty middle where the lap is made in the corners rather than on the power: Antonelli finally found his front end and went within a few thousandths of Verstappen through it. The Hungaroring is essentially one long second sector. A car that can shadow a Red Bull through the bends at Spa is not a car that turns up to Budapest afraid. He is the bookmakers' favourite, he is the form driver, and this was meant to be the weekend that finally exposed the Mercedes. It may not lay a finger on it.

McLaren's title defence, now with homework

Spare a thought for the reigning champion. Lando Norris is fifth, 101 points behind a lead he is supposed to be defending, and yet the Hungaroring ought to be McLaren's garden: they have won the last two here, Norris in 2025 and Oscar Piastri in 2024. The catch is that this year's car has a low-speed-corner problem, which is exactly the wrong flaw to bring to a track made almost entirely of slow and medium corners. Hence the upgrades: a new floor, plus a rotating "Macarena" rear wing they intend to try on Friday and then, apparently, not race. It is the last chance to learn what the thing actually is before summer swallows three weeks.

The gamblers' last homework

Because everyone treats Hungary as the final assignment before the holidays, the upgrade trucks arrived full. Aston Martin, second from bottom with a single point to Fernando Alonso's name, bring an Adrian Newey-designed B-spec so extensive it needed a fresh crash test to be legal, the biggest single roll of the dice of their season. Red Bull bring back the wing they abandoned at Spa, on a track that will finally tell them whether it works. Everyone wants a good number to sit on for three weeks.

Where it leaves us

So: a runaway leader on the one track that ought to test his car, a Ferrari that has run out of excuses, a champion trying to remember how it is done, and a midfield flinging parts at the wall before the beach. Overtaking has always been hard, though the new cars might yet have a say, so watch qualifying regardless. A one-stop usually wins, so watch the strategy. Session times, live and in your own timezone, are on the weekend page, and the race is on F1 TV on Sunday. After that, nothing until Zandvoort on 23 August. This is the last flag before F1 goes quiet, and Antonelli would love a comfortable one. The Hungaroring rarely obliges.

title.raw: Fast and fragile: Ferrari top a wild Hungary FP1 as Aston's new car breaks on debut
title.rendered: Fast and fragile: Ferrari top a wild Hungary FP1 as Aston’s new car breaks on debut

content.raw:
All week the story was the same one: Ferrari had run out of excuses at a track built to flatter them, and this was finally the weekend to make good on the hopium. It took them one session to start. Charles Leclerc topped first practice, Max Verstappen wedged his Red Bull between the two red cars, and Lewis Hamilton made it a Ferrari one-three. Then, with seven minutes left, Leclerc coasted to a halt in the pit lane. Fast and fragile, and that was only half the drama, because the session's red flag belonged to an Aston Martin that broke before it had properly turned a wheel. Enjoy the hopium. Just keep a hand on your wallet.

The order

Leclerc went round in 1:19.075 and left the rest to squabble over the scraps, half a second clear on a lap that barely lasts eighty seconds. The Dutchman was the best of them at 0.484 back, grumbling about "horrendous" downshifts on the radio and going second anyway. Isack Hadjar put the other Red Bull fourth and pipped George Russell's Mercedes by 0.069, the French prodigy once again outdriving reputations twice the size of his. The eye-catcher was seventh: Frederik Vesti, standing in for the championship leader, quicker than most of the men who race these cars for a living. Audi bracketed him, Gabriel Bortoleto sixth and Nico Hülkenberg eighth. Nice while it lasts.

The sting in the tail

Ferrari's morning came with a scare bolted to it. Leclerc had barely banked his headline lap when he was back on the radio reporting that "something broke", coasting into the pit lane with what looked like a gearbox problem and seven minutes still to run. It did not cost him top spot, but it turned an hour of pure encouragement into one of reassurance and worry in roughly equal measure. The pace is plainly there. Whether the thing survives a Sunday is suddenly a live question, which is not a sentence Ferrari supporters enjoy reading in July.

Read the trap, not the clock

Here is the part that should worry the rest. Down the speed trap, Lando Norris was fastest at 327 km/h and Verstappen next at 326. The two Ferraris went through at 318 and 319, down among the very slowest on the grid with only the two Aston Martins below them. On any other weekend that is a headline and a problem. Here it is a footnote. The Hungaroring is fourteen corners and one straight worth the name, Monaco without the walls, and it could not care less how fast your car goes in a line it barely owns. It rewards a car that can roll one medium-speed corner into the next without upsetting itself, which is exactly what the Ferrari has done all season. Slowest in a straight line and quickest on the lap is not a paradox at this place. It is the job description.

The rocketship stayed in the garage

The strangest thing about the timesheet is who is not on it. Kimi Antonelli leads the championship by 45 points and did not turn a competitive lap all hour, because Friday morning was young-driver duty and Toto's rocketship spent it parked while Vesti brought it up to temperature. Five teams did the same: Vesti for Antonelli, Leonardo Fornaroli for Oscar Piastri at McLaren, Ryo Hirakawa for Oliver Bearman at Haas, Paul Aron for Franco Colapinto at Alpine, and Colton Herta for Valtteri Bottas at Cadillac. A quarter of the usual front of the grid, in other words, sat this one out, which is your cue to hold the whole order at arm's length and to trust nothing the midfield did.

Newey's big bet breaks on arrival

Which brings us to the car everyone came to see. Aston Martin rolled into Budapest with the biggest single upgrade anyone has brought all year, the Newey B-spec, a near-total rework of the machine: new front wing, a longer and thinner nose, every permitted floor surface touched, a new diffuser, a new three-element rear wing, sixteen parts in all, the lot built up in a frantic overnight thrash. It lasted about half an hour. Thirty-six minutes in, the rear of Lance Stroll's brand-new car let go on the exit of Turn 2, spun him through 360 degrees and brought out the session's only red flag. He climbed out unhurt, which is the good news. The bad news is the rest of it: a suspected suspension failure on the debut of the most expensive gamble of their season, six minutes of everyone's running gone, and a wary Fernando Alonso sent back out under orders to keep the thing off the kerbs. He managed thirteenth, Stroll never ran again and was classified twenty-first. The trap numbers, 302 and 303 km/h and flat last, tell you they have bolted on every gram of downforce the new floor will carry. Whether it is quick is a question for a car that stays in one piece. Ask again this afternoon.

McLaren, doing quiet homework

Norris was eleventh, the wrong side of two seconds off Leclerc, which is not where a reigning champion wants to be at a track McLaren have won at two years running. Their car has a low-speed-corner weakness, which at a circuit built almost entirely of slow and medium corners is the worst possible flaw to pack for the trip, and the new floor they brought, the first slice of a two-part package that finishes at Zandvoort, is aimed squarely at it. They handed Fornaroli's car the job of trialling their "Macarena" rear wing, their own read on Ferrari's upside-down concept, and pronounced it to be working well, even as they confirmed they will not race it here or in Holland. Friday morning did not exactly sell the package. Then again, McLaren mumbling through a Friday and then conjuring half a second on Saturday is one of the sport's oldest routines, and Piastri's car spent the hour on rookie duty. Eleventh earns a shrug, not a headline. For now.

Asterisks before the beach

Beyond the stand-ins, this was a scruffy hour. The stewards spent most of it binning lap times, Turn 1 and Turn 7 the repeat offenders, with Russell, Alexander Albon and Carlos Sainz among the guilty. Sainz had the morning from hell: last of the twenty-two, a fistful of deleted laps, a lurid lock-up into Turn 1 that very nearly ended in the wall, and a summons to the stewards alongside Verstappen over an earlier traffic incident. And the long-run data, the one genuinely useful thing a Friday usually hands you, was too broken up to mean much, short runs on mixed tyres either side of the stoppage. Nobody managed a race simulation worth the name. That, and a track temperature that actually resembles Sunday's, is what the afternoon is for.

What to watch in FP2

Second practice is the one that counts, run this afternoon in the heat, far closer to what Saturday and Sunday will ask, and with all twenty race drivers finally back in their own cars. Five things worth your eyes:

  • Ferrari's health, not their speed. The pace looks real; the worry does not go away on its own. Watch whether Leclerc's car is fixed and whether the Ferrari can string a long run together without crying off. Do both and the hopium is earned.
  • Whether Aston actually has a car. They gathered next to nothing this morning. Can they rebuild Stroll's, keep both cars off the kerbs, and prove the sixteen parts add pace rather than only downforce and drag. This afternoon is effectively their first practice of the weekend.
  • McLaren with the grown-ups back. Piastri returns, the new floor gets a real run, and we learn whether that two-second-looking gap is genuine or the usual Friday theatre.
  • The actual rocketship. Antonelli climbs back in, and Russell reckons the deployment gremlin that hobbled Mercedes at Spa and Silverstone is finally solved, which should sharpen them on the straights and let them simply drive. If the leader turns up quick, the corner myth dies in a hurry.
  • A first honest pecking order. Long runs and qualifying simulations on a representative track, at a one-stop circuit where race pace tends to decide Sunday. Watch the tyres, watch Turns 1 and 7, and watch who has something genuinely in hand.

The real timesheet starts now. Session times in your own timezone, and the order as it firms up, live on the weekend page.

title.raw: Hamilton Leads a Ferrari one-two in a red flagged FP2
title.rendered: Hamilton Leads a Ferrari one-two in a red flagged FP2

content.raw:
If first practice was a rumour, the afternoon started filling in the details. Lewis Hamilton led a Ferrari one-two in FP2, a tenth and a half clear of Charles Leclerc, and this time the red cars were quick everywhere rather than only through the corners. The hopium has stopped being a punchline and started looking like a problem for everyone else. It was not a tidy hour: Franco Colapinto put his Alpine in the barriers, Lance Stroll never made it out of the garage at all, and the championship leader spent his afternoon trying not to spin. But the top of the timesheet could not have been redder.

Hamilton doing Hamilton things at the Hamiltonring

Hamilton has spent the best part of two decades treating the Hungaroring as a second home, and a 1:18.729 on a set of soft tyres already six laps old is the kind of lap that says he still means it. It did not come easy. Leclerc had gone quickest with a 1:18.877 inside the closing twenty minutes, only for the seven-time champion to snatch it back with the very next effort. Two Ferraris, three tenths clear of everyone else, at a circuit built to reward precisely what their car does best. For the first time this season, "Ferrari are the team to beat" is a sentence you can say without a laugh track.

No issues for Ferrari

The FP1 sting, Leclerc coasting to a halt with a suspected gearbox, did not repeat itself. Both cars ran clean for the full hour, and the straight-line worry from the morning quietly disappeared with them: Hamilton and Leclerc went through the speed trap at 327 and 326 km/h, right in the pack rather than propping up the field the way they had before lunch. Quick through the corners was never in doubt. Quick in a straight line and reliable for a full session is how a promising Friday turns into a threat.

Difficulty settling in for Kimi, Russell struggles to 5th

If the morning's oddity was Kimi Antonelli watching a rookie warm up his car, the afternoon's was the championship leader climbing back in and going backwards. Antonelli was thirteenth, nearly two seconds off Hamilton, his session a catalogue of lock-ups, a couple of near-spins under braking and a mistake in the final sector that threw away his best lap. Mercedes offered to take some front wing out to settle the rear; he was not sold. George Russell did better in fifth and still climbed out complaining of an "extremely bad" feeling from the car. The Hungaroring is doing to the silver cars exactly what everyone promised it would: removing the one thing they are best at and putting a magnifying glass over everything they are not. Forty-five points still cushion Antonelli at the top of the standings, and a scruffy Friday does not dent that, but it was nobody's idea of a statement.

McLaren, as promised

McLaren mumbling through a Friday and then conjuring half a second is one of the sport's oldest routines, and right on cue, Lando Norris hauled the McLaren up to third, best of the non-Ferraris and a different postcode from the eleventh a rookie-shared FP1 had left him in. The new floor got a proper run, Oscar Piastri was back in the other car in eighth, and the low-speed-corner weakness that was supposed to sink them here looked a good deal more manageable once the track warmed up. Not a Ferrari. But the closest thing to one.

Colapinto's error

The red flag belonged to Colapinto. Just before half-distance the Alpine snapped away from him on the entry to the final corner and speared backwards into the barriers, wrecking the rear of the car in a stiff crosswind on a surface that had been dusty and mean all day. He climbed out unhurt; the car will need a new back end. The timing was cruel for everyone else, because the stoppage dropped right into the middle of the soft-tyre qualifying runs. Piastri and Antonelli were among those who never got a clean lap in afterwards, which is worth holding on to before anyone reads the order behind the Ferraris as gospel.

No FP2 for Stroll, more disappointment at Aston Martin

Spare another thought for Aston Martin. Their morning ended with Stroll's brand-new car pitching him into a spin on a suspected rear-suspension failure. Their afternoon did not happen: the team could not repair the damage in time, so Stroll sat out FP2 completely and was classified last, having managed eleven laps of his sixteen-part gamble in the whole day. Adrian Newey, the man whose name is on the project, conceded the team were "short on spares" and that the failure was "very unexpected", which is not a sentence you want from your technical figurehead on debut day. There was a sliver of light: in Fernando Alonso's hands the new car looked a genuine step, hauling Aston back among the Cadillacs at the tail rather than stranded behind them. Progress, of a sort, measured from rock bottom and gathered on a single car.

No Race Pace Data

The one thing FP2 could not hand over was a clean look at race pace. Colapinto's crash gutted the long-run phase, so the tyre-wear picture that usually makes a Friday worth studying is half-drawn at best. On a single fast lap the message is blunt: Ferrari, then a gap, then the rest. Over a stint, nobody can honestly say yet, and anyone who tells you otherwise is guessing.

Where it leaves us

So Ferrari roll into Saturday as clear favourites for a pole that, at this circuit, is usually worth more than any clever strategy. Hamilton has the happy memories and, today, the fastest car; Leclerc has the FP1 headline and a score to settle; between them they have turned a season of hopium into something that looks a lot like expectation. Antonelli still leads by 45 and would dearly like to remember how to string a lap together before it matters. Third practice and qualifying come on Saturday, and the running order, live and in your own timezone, sits on the weekend page. The hopium has a stopwatch behind it now. That part is new.

title.raw: The hiding is over: Norris tops final practice as McLaren finally show their hand
title.rendered: The hiding is over: Norris tops final practice as McLaren finally show their hand

content.raw:
We flagged it on Friday: eleventh in first practice for the reigning champion, a raised eyebrow rather than a red pen, because McLaren hiding on a Friday and then finding half a second on Saturday is the sport's oldest routine. Right on schedule, Lando Norris put the McLaren on top of final practice, a 1:17.939 that left Lewis Hamilton's Ferrari 0.117 behind and the rest of the front-runners bunched up in his wake.

The order arrives

Kimi Antonelli slotted third for Mercedes, a hundredth off Hamilton, with Charles Leclerc fourth and Oscar Piastri fifth to keep both Ferraris and both McLarens inside the top five. George Russell was sixth. The notable name lower down was Max Verstappen, seventh and seven tenths adrift, the Red Bull looking like exactly the handful its driver keeps describing at a track that punishes a car for being anything less than planted.

What it told us

Not much that Friday had not already hinted at, and everything the paddock suspected. The new floor McLaren brought to fix their low-speed-corner problem looked like it had done its job; the car that could barely see the road in the morning session was suddenly the one to beat once the track came to it. Ferrari, quick all weekend through the corners and short on the straights, stayed in the fight. The final hour before qualifying rarely lies, and this one pointed squarely at a McLaren-Ferrari front row. Whether the low-fuel headline pace survived into the session that counts was, as ever at the Hungaroring, the only question that mattered. Session times, live and in your own timezone, sit on the weekend page.
