title.raw: Norris steals it by a whisker, then the stewards redraw the grid: Hungary qualifying
title.rendered: Norris steals it by a whisker, then the stewards redraw the grid: Hungary qualifying

content.raw:
Qualifying at the Hungaroring gave us the closest thing to a fair fight all weekend, and then handed the result to a committee. On track, Lando Norris produced a 1:17.207 to snatch pole from Lewis Hamilton by twelve thousandths of a second, his first pole of a season he is supposed to be leading. Hamilton had provisionally taken it; the reigning champion found the margin on his final run and took it back. A brilliant lap, a brilliant session, and for about an hour a genuinely mouthwatering front row.

Then qualifying moved indoors

The stewards were busy. First, Hamilton was handed a three-place grid penalty for impeding Oscar Piastri at Turn 1 in Q3, the Ferrari sitting on the racing line and forcing the McLaren wide and off its lap. Second, championship leader Kimi Antonelli, who had qualified fourth, copped his own three-place drop for failing to slow enough under the yellow flags thrown when Max Verstappen spun his Red Bull in Q3. Two separate offences, two identical sanctions, and a grid that looked nothing like the timesheet by the time the paperwork cleared.

The grid it left behind

Norris keeps pole, untouched. The big winner is Charles Leclerc, promoted onto the front row in second by Hamilton's demotion, an all-red second row becoming a McLaren-Ferrari one. Piastri inherits third, Verstappen climbs to fourth from a genuine sixth, and Hamilton drops to fifth on a day he might have started second. George Russell lines up sixth, and Antonelli, who was fourth on merit, starts seventh, a needless self-inflicted step back for a man carrying a championship lead into the summer.

Why any of this matters

Because it is the Hungaroring, and the Hungaroring does not do overtaking. A grid penalty here is not a minor inconvenience to be undone on Sunday; it is, more often than not, the race. Norris starts where he wants to be. Ferrari, the team everyone spent the week fancying, put a car on the front row and left another wounded in fifth. And the championship leader begins from seventh at a track where seventh tends to stay seventh. The stopwatch had its say. Then the stewards had theirs. Sunday's race, and where the standings sit after it, are on the weekend page.

title.raw: F1 Hungary Grand Prix 2026: Norris takes it as Antonelli lands podium to extend lead
title.rendered: F1 Hungary Grand Prix 2026: Norris takes it as Antonelli lands podium to extend lead

content.raw:
Two Fridays running we have said it: McLaren mumbling through practice and then finding half a second on Saturday is one of the sport's oldest routines. This time they ran the full act. Lando Norris sat eleventh in FP1, said nothing, then took FP3, pole and the race. His first win of the season he is supposed to be defending, at the track everyone had already handed to somebody else.

He called his shot

The middle of this race was an argument, and Norris won it twice. Stuck behind Oscar Piastri, who had taken the lead fair and square with a lovely cutback at Turn 2 on lap one, Norris got on the radio and demanded to stop first. McLaren refused. So the reigning champion, with exactly the ego the job description asks for, told his engineer what would happen instead: "I'll pull out a 10-second gap with no tyres."

He then did precisely that. Piastri stopped first on lap 33, Norris stayed out on rubber older than some race seats, and by the time the maths settled he did not need the ten seconds anyway: the margin was 15. Piastri's luck ran out early, and for all the talk of equal machinery, his Sunday pace was nothing like his team mate's. When the virtual safety car arrived, Norris took his second stop for free and drove off into the summer. Ordered only to stay off the kerbs, the team nursing reliability worries he never let show, he won by 15.080 seconds with two deleted lap times for enthusiasm.

Monaco without the walls, and backmarkers everywhere

Now the ugly part. This was one of the most dreadful blue-flag races we have seen, and it decided the lead. On lap 38 Carlos Sainz, a lap down and fighting Fernando Alonso for fourteenth like it was the world championship, tried a move around the outside into Turn 2, failed, and cut back across the race leader. Piastri went to the grass, the lead went with him.

Sainz reached for the excuses and there are none. His steering wheel may not have lit up, the GPS gremlins were real enough, but the marshals' panels waved blue at him repeatedly and his own pit wall had told him Piastri was coming. The stewards wrote it down in black and white: he "had been informed by the team that blue flags were being shown", and he was "wholly responsible" for the contact. The only reason the standard ten seconds became five is that they accepted Piastri sat in his blind spot. He was told, he chose to keep racing Alonso, and he collected the leader of the grand prix. We know the Hungaroring is Monaco without the walls and overtakes do not come cheap here, but contact with the man leading the race is uncalled for. Appalling, honestly.

Piastri's radio said it better than any steward: "Get out of the f****** way you idiot." Afterwards he called it one of the dumbest things he had ever seen on a racetrack, and suggested a man so free with criticism of others "should look in the mirror a bit". He was not the only victim of the blue-flag shambles either: Oliver Bearman took five seconds for ignoring them, lapped traffic kept wandering into the podium fight, and Toto Wolff went on television calling race engineers "Teletubbies". Not the sport's finest Sunday.

Valid emotions

Piastri had a second grievance and, we would argue, a fair one. His sarcasm at his own pit wall, "nice of you guys to factor that one in by the way, thanks", landed on a team that has won the constructors' championship two years running and somehow could not work out that a car leaving the pits at the Hungaroring lands in traffic. Valid emotions. Andrea Stella called it a comment made in anger and Piastri himself conceded you do not plan a strategy around being taken out by a backmarker, but the out-lap into that mess is exactly the variable a back-to-back champion team is paid to see coming.

It did not matter for long. On lap 56 the gearbox let go and the McLaren rolled to a stop before Turn 3, bringing out the VSC that gift-wrapped Norris's pit stop. Led half the race, hit by a backmarker, retired by his own car. A genuinely dreadful Sunday, and his plan for the break was the only sensible line left: reset, and find some pace.

The anxiety of watching Max

Max Verstappen's weekend was a fan-anxiety machine. Friday was "a lot of complaints", Saturday he spun in Q3 and called the car not driveable and getting worse, and all of it on the same rear wing that has already failed him once this season. When a driver of his stature keeps dropping it at track after track with the same specification bolted on, you know it is nothing close to driver error. Even Red Bull's technical chief Pierre Waché admits the data cannot keep up with the driver: the things Max feels through the steering wheel, the team cannot detect in the simulator. That gap between his hands and their screens is now Red Bull's most important engineering project.

And then, on Sunday, second place. Best of the mortals by a distance, a fourth podium of the season and a third in the last four races, seasoned with the overtake of the afternoon: the dive down the inside of Lewis Hamilton at Turn 1 on lap 16, the kind of move that makes you forget the car under him is held together by feedback the factory cannot measure. He and Hamilton gave us a proper race for the podium places, which is more than most of the field managed.

Ferrari, undone by a decimal

Charles Leclerc finished fourth, right behind the team mate who out-qualified him by twelve thousandths on Saturday. On the road Hamilton crossed the line 4.3 seconds ahead of the sister car; then the stewards applied five seconds for speeding in the pit lane by 0.1 km/h, and fourth became fifth. Harsh? The margin, yes. The penalty, no. Pit-lane speeding is a slam dunk, the amount has never mattered, and Hamilton knows it better than anyone on this grid. A weekend that started twelve thousandths from pole ended demoted by a decimal.

Mercedes, split screen

Kimi Antonelli once again did what he does best: turned up at a circuit where Mercedes had no real pace and left with a podium anyway. Third place, the championship lead intact, and the gap over Hamilton in second stretched to a round 50 points as the paddock packs for the beach. That is the cushion of a champion in waiting, built one unglamorous podium at a time.

George Russell, meanwhile, triggered his own anti-stall at the lights and fell to twenty-first before Turn 1 mattered. He spent 70 laps working it back to seventh, the last car on the lead lap as Norris hoovered up everyone from Liam Lawson in eighth backwards. A good recovery drive and nothing more, which at this point surprises nobody.

The rest of the points, and the fires

Isack Hadjar banked a beautiful sixth, spending the closing stint defending against cars on far fresher rubber, Russell's tyres twelve laps younger by the flag, and never cracking. Lawson's eighth, with Arvid Lindblad tenth, pushed Racing Bulls past Alpine in the constructors' table, 66 points to 61, after the two had arrived in Hungary dead level. Between them sat Nico Hülkenberg, ninth after relieving Lindblad of the place on lap 63, and onto the scoreboard for the first time all season: Audi's first cheer of a long year.

Honest word for Aston Martin too. Practice was a mess, but qualifying and especially the race were as tidy as their season gets, Lance Stroll and Alonso bringing both cars home thirteenth and fourteenth in a 70-lap race of attrition. Alpine, Williams and Haas, by contrast, were simply not there.

And then Cadillac. Valtteri Bottas's brakes decided their lifecycle was complete on lap 16, the left front catching fire and the Finn using the pit wall to slow the car on his way in, which is one way to test week-old bodywork. The bitter joke: the team had brought new brake ducts to Hungary to fix exactly this. Sergio Pérez, who had already started from the pit lane after overnight changes, lost the suspension on lap 51. A double DNF, again, and a summer break with a very clear to-do list.

Where it leaves us

Top ten: 1. Norris (McLaren), 2. Verstappen (Red Bull), 3. Antonelli (Mercedes), 4. Leclerc (Ferrari), 5. Hamilton (Ferrari), 6. Hadjar (Red Bull), 7. Russell (Mercedes), 8. Lawson (Racing Bulls), 9. Hülkenberg (Audi), 10. Lindblad (Racing Bulls). (Full classification.)

For the books: Norris's 12th career win, his first repeat win at any circuit, his first with the number 1 on the car, McLaren's 204th, and their third Hungarian Grand Prix on the bounce. Antonelli carries a 50-point lead over Hamilton into the break; Norris, for all Sunday's noise, is still only fifth, behind both Ferraris. The grid disappears until Zandvoort on 23 August. The sandbag paid off. The question for everyone chasing is whether it was the track, the tyres or the truth.

title.raw: F1 Hungarian Grand Prix 2026, lap by lap: the Hungaroring race in order
title.rendered: F1 Hungarian Grand Prix 2026, lap by lap: the Hungaroring race in order

content.raw:
Two McLarens disappeared up the road, then one of them disappeared for good. Lando Norris won a Hungarian Grand Prix he spent half of stuck behind his team mate, via one virtual safety car, three retirements, a lap 38 collision between the leader and a backmarker, and a pit lane speeding penalty measured in decimals. Front to back, in order:

Lap 1

Oscar Piastri, third on the grid, is the mover: past Charles Leclerc off the line, then the cutback out of Turn 2 on Norris for the lead. Max Verstappen deals with the Ferraris for third while Lewis Hamilton and Leclerc swap twice before settling, Hamilton ahead. The disaster is further back: George Russell triggers his own anti-stall at the lights and the entire field streams past, the Mercedes falling to twenty-first before the lap is done. He picks off Valtteri Bottas before the line just to start the climb.

Laps 2-18: Russell climbs, the first stops, and a fire

Russell's recovery runs like a metronome: Lance Stroll and Alexander Albon on lap 2, Carlos Sainz on 3, Oliver Bearman on 4, Fernando Alonso on 5, Franco Colapinto on 6, Gabriel Bortoleto on 8, Esteban Ocon on 9, Pierre Gasly on 12, Nico Hülkenberg on 17, Arvid Lindblad on 18. Ten cars repassed on track before his first stop.

Stroll blinks first in the pit lane on lap 8, off his starting softs. Bottas never gets that far: the Cadillac's left front brake catches fire and he is out after 13 laps, slowing the car against the pit wall on his way in. Up front the leaders cycle through their first stops, Hamilton the most aggressive on lap 13, Verstappen 14, Piastri and Leclerc 16, Norris 17. On lap 16, mid-cycle, Verstappen goes down the inside of Hamilton at Turn 1, the pass of the afternoon, having taken Liam Lawson the same lap.

Laps 19-33: the argument

Piastri leads Norris by roughly a second and the race settles into a McLaren radio drama. Norris demands to stop first; McLaren refuse; Norris promises a 10-second gap on old tyres instead. Kimi Antonelli runs a long first stint to lap 22, Russell to 27. In the midfield Alonso is doing something eccentric: 34 laps on his starting softs, which holds until it doesn't, Lawson, Lindblad, Hülkenberg and Gasly all coming past between laps 24 and 27 as the rubber gives up.

Hamilton pits again on lap 30, committing to three stops. McLaren cover him with Piastri on lap 33. Norris stays out. The race turns on that.

Laps 34-40: the leader meets the traffic

Piastri rejoins on fresh hards and drives straight into a war for fourteenth: Sainz, Bearman, Alonso, Ocon, Stroll and Colapinto trading places every lap from 36 to 40, a lap down and racing each other like the flag was theirs. On lap 38, at Turn 3, Sainz cuts back across the McLaren after a failed move on Alonso and they touch, Piastri onto the grass. The stewards later rule Sainz wholly responsible, five seconds, softened from ten only because Piastri sat in his blind spot. Alonso, on his fresh mediums, re-passes the whole cluster on laps 37 to 39 for good measure.

The time Piastri loses in that mess is the undercut-proofing Norris never got from his own pit wall. When the second stops shake out, the champion is effectively in front.

Laps 41-55: the long game

Verstappen stops on lap 41 and takes softs, 29 laps to the flag on the red tyre, a call nobody copies. Isack Hadjar covers him a lap later. Sergio Pérez, who started from the pit lane after overnight changes, loses the suspension and parks on lap 48, Cadillac's second retirement. Antonelli makes his second stop on lap 53, Russell on 54, both onto hards. Norris still has not stopped a second time. He is 22 laps into rubber the pit wall keeps asking about, telling them the gap will come. It has: the lead is real now.

Lap 56: the gearbox and the gift

Piastri's gearbox lets go and the McLaren rolls to a stop at Turn 3 from second place. Virtual safety car. Norris, Hamilton and Leclerc pit at reduced-delta speed, the Ferraris double-stacked; Verstappen and Antonelli stay out. The order out the other side: Norris leading on fresh softs, Verstappen second, Antonelli third after Hamilton loses the pit-exit race to the Mercedes, Leclerc fifth behind his team mate. The VSC ends on lap 57 having lasted barely a lap and decided the podium.

Laps 57-70: run to the flag

Norris clears off, 15.080 seconds in hand at the line despite a deleted lap on 60 for track limits. Leclerc sets the fastest lap of the race on 58, a 1:22.000, chasing a Hamilton he cannot pass. Hamilton spends the closing laps harrying Antonelli's older hards for the podium and never quite gets there, and on lap 61 the stewards note him for pit lane speeding, 0.1 km/h over. The five seconds land on lap 66 and quietly hand fourth to Leclerc, 0.7 the classified gap. No pass required.

The last points move on track: Lawson takes Lindblad on lap 63 and Hülkenberg follows through on 64, Audi's first points of the season sealed at the expense of the rookie who had held ninth. Bortoleto, black-and-white flagged for track limits on the final lap, stays eleventh.

Pit log (44 stops)

Two-stoppers won it, mostly by accident: Norris ran laps 18-56 on one set of hards because the VSC made his second stop free. Hamilton and Leclerc both three-stopped (13/30/56 and 16/36/56). Verstappen's 29-lap soft stint to the flag was the boldest tyre call of the day; Antonelli's lap 53 stop, three laps before the VSC, the unluckiest. Stroll stopped earliest (lap 8); Alonso ran his opening softs to lap 34.

Retirements

  • Lap 13 Bottas (Cadillac), front-left brake fire.
  • Lap 48 Pérez (Cadillac), suspension, after a pit lane start.
  • Lap 55 Piastri (McLaren), gearbox, from second, having led laps 1-33.

Where it leaves the title

Antonelli keeps the championship lead into the summer break, 50 points over Hamilton; Norris's first win of the season lifts the champion to fifth. Full classification. Next: Zandvoort, 23 August.

Lap-by-lap movements are from OpenF1 timing; overtake coverage is not exhaustive.

On lap 16, mid-cycle, Verstappen goes down the inside of Hamilton at Turn 1, the pass of the afternoon, having taken Liam Lawson the same lap.

Laps 19-33: the argument

Piastri leads Norris by roughly a second and the race settles into a McLaren radio drama. Norris demands to stop first; McLaren refuse; Norris promises a 10-second gap on old tyres instead. Kimi Antonelli runs a long first stint to lap 22, Russell to 27. In the midfield Alonso is doing something eccentric: 34 laps on his starting softs, which holds until it doesn’t, Lawson, Lindblad, Hülkenberg and Gasly all coming past between laps 24 and 27 as the rubber gives up.

Hamilton pits again on lap 30, committing to three stops. McLaren cover him with Piastri on lap 33. Norris stays out. The race turns on that.

Laps 34-40: the leader meets the traffic

Piastri rejoins on fresh hards and drives straight into a war for fourteenth: Sainz, Bearman, Alonso, Ocon, Stroll and Colapinto trading places every lap from 36 to 40, a lap down and racing each other like the flag was theirs. On lap 38, at Turn 3, Sainz cuts back across the McLaren after a failed move on Alonso and they touch, Piastri onto the grass. The stewards later rule Sainz wholly responsible, five seconds, softened from ten only because Piastri sat in his blind spot. Alonso, on his fresh mediums, re-passes the whole cluster on laps 37 to 39 for good measure.

The time Piastri loses in that mess is the undercut-proofing Norris never got from his own pit wall. When the second stops shake out, the champion is effectively in front.

Laps 41-55: the long game

Verstappen stops on lap 41 and takes softs, 29 laps to the flag on the red tyre, a call nobody copies. Isack Hadjar covers him a lap later. Sergio Pérez, who started from the pit lane after overnight changes, loses the suspension and parks on lap 48, Cadillac’s second retirement. Antonelli makes his second stop on lap 53, Russell on 54, both onto hards. Norris still has not stopped a second time. He is 22 laps into rubber the pit wall keeps asking about, telling them the gap will come. It has: the lead is real now.

Lap 56: the gearbox and the gift

Piastri’s gearbox lets go and the McLaren rolls to a stop at Turn 3 from second place. Virtual safety car. Norris, Hamilton and Leclerc pit at reduced-delta speed, the Ferraris double-stacked; Verstappen and Antonelli stay out. The order out the other side: Norris leading on fresh softs, Verstappen second, Antonelli third after Hamilton loses the pit-exit race to the Mercedes, Leclerc fifth behind his team mate. The VSC ends on lap 57 having lasted barely a lap and decided the podium.

Laps 57-70: run to the flag

Norris clears off, 15.080 seconds in hand at the line despite a deleted lap on 60 for track limits. Leclerc sets the fastest lap of the race on 58, a 1:22.000, chasing a Hamilton he cannot pass. Hamilton spends the closing laps harrying Antonelli’s older hards for the podium and never quite gets there, and on lap 61 the stewards note him for pit lane speeding, 0.1 km/h over. The five seconds land on lap 66 and quietly hand fourth to Leclerc, 0.7 the classified gap. No pass required.

The last points move on track: Lawson takes Lindblad on lap 63 and Hülkenberg follows through on 64, Audi’s first points of the season sealed at the expense of the rookie who had held ninth. Bortoleto, black-and-white flagged for track limits on the final lap, stays eleventh.

Pit log (44 stops)

Two-stoppers won it, mostly by accident: Norris ran laps 18-56 on one set of hards because the VSC made his second stop free. Hamilton and Leclerc both three-stopped (13/30/56 and 16/36/56). Verstappen’s 29-lap soft stint to the flag was the boldest tyre call of the day; Antonelli’s lap 53 stop, three laps before the VSC, the unluckiest. Stroll stopped earliest (lap 8); Alonso ran his opening softs to lap 34.

Retirements

  • Lap 13 Bottas (Cadillac), front-left brake fire.
  • Lap 48 Pérez (Cadillac), suspension, after a pit lane start.
  • Lap 55 Piastri (McLaren), gearbox, from second, having led laps 1-33.

Where it leaves the title

Antonelli keeps the championship lead into the summer break, 50 points over Hamilton; Norris’s first win of the season lifts the champion to fifth. Full classification. Next: Zandvoort, 23 August.

Lap-by-lap movements are from OpenF1 timing; overtake coverage is not exhaustive.

content.raw:
By Παναγιώτης Λουτριώτης

From pole, but not into the lead

After the qualifying where the Ferraris and the McLarens showed their strength around this track, the defending champion Lando Norris was starting from pole. The grid penalties of Antonelli and Hamilton left Charles Leclerc to complete the front row. But the lead of the race wasn't earned by either of them but by the McLaren of Oscar Piastri, who launched himself from P3 to the top at the first turns of the race. A great start was also made by Max Verstappen. The 4-time world champion took advantage of the grid penalties and, starting from P4, made the move on Leclerc's Ferrari to climb onto the podium. Some problem on Russell's Mercedes put the engine on anti-stall, making the British driver's start a total disaster as he fell all the way to the bottom.

The first stops

In the next laps we got what we expected, a strategic, few-overtake race, the exception was Russell, who got some positions back trying to save his race. Verstappen was holding the Ferraris (with the soft compound) behind him as the McLaren at the top was creating space from the rest. Norris was complaining to the team that his teammate was much slower and he was wasting his time. This was happening until lap 13, when Ferrari decided to pit Hamilton in an attempt to undercut Verstappen. In his outlap the 7-time world champion had to clear both of the RBs and the Red Bull of Isack Hadjar to increase his possibilities to step on the podium. At turn 5 he cleared Lindblad round the outside with some incredible driving using his fresh rubber. On the next lap Max was called in to avoid getting undercut, something that didn't happen as he rejoined behind Hamilton.

The overtake of the season

The race continued with a retirement in the pit lane by Bottas, whose brakes caught fire, this incident delayed Piastri's pit stop by a lap. All this back and forth between Hamilton and Verstappen resulted in the highlight of the race: on the start-finish straight both drivers were clearing Lawson, when Max decided to dive-bomb Lewis at turn 1 from miles back, gaining the position. One of the best overtakes of the season, at the expense of one of the most talented (if not the most) drivers on the grid, on a track that is not so friendly to overtakes.

The second stops

After every race contender had pitted (except Antonelli), the McLarens, the Ferraris and Max were stuck behind Hadjar, who had not pitted yet. With the first pit window over, the lap 1 positions had been restored. On lap 30 Ferrari decided to pit Hamilton early as an opportunity to hunt even the first place, to which McLaren responded by pitting the leader of the race and freeing space for Norris to run outside his teammate's dirty air, which he was complaining about in the team radios.

The contact that cost Piastri the lead

On lap 38 Oscar was starting to find pace with his fresh tyres and clearing some backmarkers, when Carlos Sainz didn't let Piastri through, which resulted in contact between the cars and the Spaniard getting a 5-second penalty. By staying out while Piastri stopped, Norris came out in front of his teammate and took the title of the favourite to win the race.

Piastri's race unravels

The other Cadillac was forced to be the second retirement of the race after Perez broke the front left suspension, but the Mexican was able to return it to the garage without the need for a VSC. After the incident with Sainz, harmful for his possibilities for the race win, disaster struck again for the young Australian driver as his gearbox betrayed him and forced him to retire from what was about to be his best race this season.

The VSC, and a penalty for Hamilton

This incident resulted in a VSC where the leader, Norris, pitted, but he had created a gap big enough to stay in the lead. Hamilton pitted too and rejoined in front of the championship leader, but the Ferrari pit wall saw that at the safety car line the Italian was in front and informed Lewis to hand the position back, instructions that he followed. But this was not the only time rules were used against the 7-time world champion, as he was penalized with a 5-second penalty for speeding in the pit lane; this is the third consecutive race that Lewis gets a penalty.

The final order

At the end Lando Norris got his first win as a world champion, and deservingly so. Max Verstappen got his second consecutive podium as Kimi Antonelli completed the podium in a race where he extended his championship lead. Ferrari 4-5 with Leclerc at P4 because of Hamilton's penalty, the other Red Bull finished in 6th place as Russell recovered from his bad start to P7. Double points for Racing Bulls as their drivers finished in P8 and P10, and Nico Hulkenberg got his first points in an Audi uniform after he finished in 9th place. For the out-of-the-points notable stuff, Aston Martin with their 16 upgrades finished 13-14, very promising for the remainder of the season. And the race for the 5th place in the constructors seems to slip away from Alpine, which ended the race pointless. (Full classification.)

content.raw:
By Stylianos Christopoulos

Ένα τριήμερο που κρίθηκε σε δύο σημεία: σε έναν ασύρματο και σε ένα κιβώτιο ταχυτήτων. Ο Lando Norris είπε στην ομάδα του ότι θα άνοιγε κενό δέκα δευτερολέπτων με φθαρμένα ελαστικά, το έκανε, και τερμάτισε πρώτος με 15.080. Ο Oscar Piastri ηγήθηκε για 33 γύρους, δέχτηκε επαφή από έναν ουραγό και μετά τον πρόδωσε το ίδιο του το μονοθέσιο. Πάμε ομάδα προς ομάδα, με το μπλοκάκι ανοιχτό.

MERCEDES

ΘΕΤΙΚΑ. Ο Kimi Antonelli ανέβηκε στο βάθρο ξεκινώντας με ποινή τριών θέσεων στο grid, την οποία πήρε επειδή δεν επιβράδυνε αρκετά στις κίτρινες σημαίες που προκάλεσε η περιστροφή του Max Verstappen στο Q3. Κράτησε το πρώτο του stint μέχρι τον 22ο γύρο και έφυγε από την Ουγγαρία με τη διαφορά του στο πρωτάθλημα στους 50 βαθμούς. Δίπλα του, ο George Russell έκανε την πιο κοπιαστική διαδρομή του Σαββατοκύριακου: μετά το anti stall στα φώτα βρέθηκε 21ος και ανέβηκε μέχρι την 7η θέση, τελευταίος στον γύρο των πρωτοπόρων. Δέκα προσπεράσεις στην πίστα, από τον Lance Stroll και τον Alexander Albon στον 2ο γύρο μέχρι τον Arvid Lindblad στον 18ο.

ΑΡΝΗΤΙΚΑ. Το anti stall μόνο του κόστισε ένα αποτέλεσμα που ήταν διαθέσιμο, γιατί ο ρυθμός υπήρχε. Και η Mercedes πλήρωσε και τον χρονισμό: έβαλε τον Antonelli στα pit στον 53ο γύρο, τρεις γύρους πριν βγει το virtual safety car. Όσοι περίμεναν, δηλαδή ο Norris και οι δύο Ferrari, έκαναν τη στάση τους σχεδόν δωρεάν. Τρεις γύροι υπομονή θα άλλαζαν το χρώμα της Κυριακής.

FERRARI

ΘΕΤΙΚΑ. Το Σάββατο η ιταλική ομάδα ήταν δώδεκα χιλιοστά από την pole, με τον Lewis Hamilton και τον Charles Leclerc στην πρώτη γραμμή του timesheet. Στον αγώνα η Ferrari ήταν η μόνη από τις μεγάλες που πήγε καθαρά σε τρεις στάσεις (Hamilton στους 13, 30 και 56, Leclerc στους 16, 36 και 56) και ο Leclerc πήρε τον ταχύτερο γύρο του αγώνα, 1:22.000 στον 58ο, μαζί με την 4η θέση.

ΑΡΝΗΤΙΚΑ. Όταν σταμάτησε το κιβώτιο του Piastri, ο Hamilton ήταν δεύτερος. Η Ferrari τον έβαλε στα pit μαζί με τον Leclerc κάτω από το virtual safety car, έχασε τη μάχη της εξόδου από τον Antonelli και βρέθηκε τέταρτος στην πίστα. Λίγο αργότερα ήρθε και το χειρότερο: ποινή πέντε δευτερολέπτων για υπέρβαση του ορίου στο pit lane κατά 0,1 km/h, που τον έριξε πίσω από τον συνοδηγό του παρότι είχε τερματίσει 4.30 δευτερόλεπτα μπροστά του. Προσθέστε και την ποινή τριών θέσεων που είχε πάρει το Σάββατο για παρεμπόδιση του Piastri στη στροφή 1 στο Q3 και έχετε ένα τριήμερο που το χάλασε μόνο του.

MCLAREN

ΘΕΤΙΚΑ. Ο Norris έκανε το σερί: FP3, pole και νίκη. Δώδεκατη νίκη καριέρας, η πρώτη του σε πίστα που είχε κερδίσει ήδη, η πρώτη με το νούμερο 1 στο μονοθέσιο, η 204η της McLaren και η τρίτη σερί στην Ουγγαρία. Στον ασύρματο ζήτησε να σταματήσει πρώτος, η ομάδα αρνήθηκε, και τους απάντησε ότι θα άνοιγε δέκα δευτερόλεπτα με παλιά ελαστικά. Έμεινε έξω μέχρι τον 56ο, πήρε τη στάση του κάτω από το VSC και τερμάτισε με 15.080 πάνω από τον δεύτερο. Ο Piastri, από την πλευρά του, πήρε την πρωτοπορία με μια καθαρή αντεπίθεση στην έξοδο της στροφής 2 στον πρώτο γύρο και την κράτησε 33 γύρους.

ΑΡΝΗΤΙΚΑ. Το ίδιο Σαββατοκύριακο έχει και τη μαύρη του σελίδα. Ο Piastri έχανε τον αγώνα του σε δύο δόσεις: πρώτα η επαφή με τον Carlos Sainz στον 38ο γύρο, μετά η βλάβη στο κιβώτιο που τον έβγαλε από τη δεύτερη θέση στον 55ο. Δύο σβησμένοι χρόνοι για τον Norris σε track limits, στους γύρους 29 και 60, δείχνουν επίσης ότι το όριο δοκιμάστηκε περισσότερο απ' όσο χρειαζόταν. Και μένει το ερώτημα της στρατηγικής: η McLaren είχε δύο μονοθέσια που μάλωναν στον ασύρματο και επέλεξε να μην παρέμβει.

RED BULL

ΘΕΤΙΚΑ. Ο Verstappen έβγαλε δεύτερη θέση από ένα μονοθέσιο που δεν εμπιστεύεται. Τέταρτο βάθρο της σεζόν, τρίτο στους τελευταίους τέσσερις αγώνες, και η κίνηση της Κυριακής δική του: βουτιά στο εσωτερικό του Hamilton στη στροφή 1 στον 16ο γύρο, στον ίδιο γύρο που πέρασε και τον Liam Lawson. Πρόσθεσε και μια επιλογή που δεν αντέγραψε κανείς, 29 γύρους με μαλακή γόμα από τον 42ο μέχρι το τέλος. Ο Isack Hadjar έκανε τη δουλειά του δεύτερου οδηγού όπως γράφεται στο βιβλίο: στάσεις στους 19 και 42, ίδιο μοτίβο με τον Verstappen, και άμυνα μέχρι το τέλος απέναντι στον Russell με ελαστικά δώδεκα γύρους νεότερα. Έκτη θέση.

ΑΡΝΗΤΙΚΑ. Η Παρασκευή ήταν «πολλά παράπονα», το Σάββατο ο Verstappen περιστράφηκε στο Q3 και χαρακτήρισε το μονοθέσιο μη οδηγήσιμο. Το πιο ανησυχητικό δεν είναι όμως η γκρίνια, είναι η παραδοχή: ο τεχνικός διευθυντής της Red Bull Pierre Waché λέει ότι όσα νιώθει ο Max μέσα από το τιμόνι δεν εμφανίζονται στα δεδομένα του simulator. Όταν ο οδηγός βλέπει κάτι που τα όργανα δεν δείχνουν, το πρόβλημα δεν είναι ο οδηγός.

RACING BULLS

ΘΕΤΙΚΑ. Διπλή βαθμολογία. Ο Lawson 8ος, ο Lindblad 10ος, και η ομάδα ανέβηκε στην 5η θέση των κατασκευαστών με 66 βαθμούς. Μπήκαν στο τριήμερο ισόπαλοι με την Alpine στους 61 και έφυγαν μπροστά.

ΑΡΝΗΤΙΚΑ. Ο Lindblad έχασε την 9η θέση στον 64ο γύρο από τον Nico Hulkenberg, δηλαδή δύο βαθμούς που ήταν στο χέρι τους. Σε μια χρονιά όπου η Racing Bulls παλεύει για την πέμπτη θέση με πέντε βαθμούς διαφορά, αυτό δεν είναι λεπτομέρεια.

ALPINE

ΘΕΤΙΚΑ. Ο Pierre Gasly ήταν ο πρώτος εκτός βαθμών, 12ος, σε ένα τριήμερο όπου η Alpine δεν είχε ρυθμό για κάτι καλύτερο. Καθαρός αγώνας, χωρίς λάθη, με ό,τι του έδωσε το μονοθέσιο.

ΑΡΝΗΤΙΚΑ. Μηδέν βαθμοί και μια πέμπτη θέση που χάθηκε την Κυριακή. Ο Franco Colapinto τερμάτισε 15ος, δύο θέσεις πίσω από τον συνοδηγό του σε ίδιο υλικό, και η Alpine φεύγει για τις διακοπές έχοντας δει τη Racing Bulls να της περνά μπροστά μέσα σε ένα απόγευμα.

HAAS

ΘΕΤΙΚΑ. Ο Esteban Ocon έφερε το μονοθέσιο στη γραμμή, 16ος, σε έναν αγώνα φθοράς όπου τρία μονοθέσια δεν τα κατάφεραν.

ΑΡΝΗΤΙΚΑ. Ο Oliver Bearman τερμάτισε 19ος με ποινή πέντε δευτερολέπτων για αγνόηση μπλε σημαιών, και το επεισόδιο του με τον Fernando Alonso στη στροφή 3 στον 3ο γύρο εξετάστηκε από τους αγωνοδίκες χωρίς περαιτέρω έρευνα. Η Haas έχει 21 βαθμούς και μοιάζει να έχει σταματήσει να προσθέτει.

AUDI

ΘΕΤΙΚΑ. Οι πρώτοι βαθμοί της χρονιάς. Ο Hulkenberg πέρασε τον Lindblad στον 64ο γύρο, τερμάτισε 9ος και έβαλε δύο βαθμούς στο κουτί της Audi μετά από δέκα αγώνες χωρίς τίποτα. Για μια ομάδα που χτίζει, η πρώτη εγγραφή στον πίνακα έχει μεγαλύτερη αξία από το μέγεθος της.

ΑΡΝΗΤΙΚΑ. Ο Gabriel Bortoleto έμεινε 11ος, μια θέση έξω από τους βαθμούς, με μονή στάση στον 29ο γύρο, και πήρε ασπρόμαυρη σημαία για track limits στον τελευταίο γύρο. Με δύο μονοθέσια στη ζώνη των βαθμών, η Audi έφυγε με το μισό.

WILLIAMS

ΘΕΤΙΚΑ. Η ταχύτερη τελική του αγώνα ήταν δική τους, με τον Sainz στα 346 km/h. Σε μια πίστα που δεν ανταμείβει την τελική ταχύτητα, είναι το μόνο που έχει η Williams να κρατήσει.

ΑΡΝΗΤΙΚΑ. Και μετά είναι το άλλο. Ο Sainz, με έναν γύρο πίσω και σε μάχη με τον Alonso για τη 14η θέση, έκοψε την πορεία του επικεφαλής του αγώνα στη στροφή 3 στον 38ο γύρο. Οι αγωνοδίκες τον έκριναν αποκλειστικά υπεύθυνο και κατέγραψαν ότι «είχε ενημερωθεί από την ομάδα ότι επιδεικνύονταν μπλε σημαίες». Τα δέκα δευτερόλεπτα έγιναν πέντε μόνο επειδή δέχτηκαν ότι ο Piastri ήταν στο τυφλό του σημείο. Τερμάτισε 18ος, τελευταίος από όσους είδαν σημαία, με τον Albon 17ο. Δίκαιο είναι να προσθέσουμε ότι το σύστημα των μπλε σημαιών είχε πρόβλημα σε όλο τον αγώνα, με τα ενδεικτικά στο τιμόνι να μην ανάβουν λόγω GPS, κάτι που έκανε τον Toto Wolff να χαρακτηρίσει «Teletubbies» τους μηχανικούς στην τηλεόραση. Πρόβλημα του συστήματος όμως δεν σημαίνει άλλοθι για επαφή με τον πρωτοπόρο.

ASTON MARTIN

ΘΕΤΙΚΑ. Το μεγαλύτερο πακέτο αναβαθμίσεων του grid: δεκαέξι νέα μέρη στα επίσημα έγγραφα παρουσίασης μονοθεσίων της FIA για τον αγώνα, μια μικρή B-spec. Και τα δύο μονοθέσια τερμάτισαν, ο Stroll 13ος και ο Alonso 14ος, σε έναν αγώνα με τρεις εγκαταλείψεις. Ο Alonso μάλιστα έβγαλε 34 γύρους με τα μαλακά ελαστικά της εκκίνησης, νούμερο που δεν πλησίασε κανείς άλλος.

ΑΡΝΗΤΙΚΑ. Δεκαέξι μέρη και κανένας βαθμός. Η Aston Martin παραμένει στον ένα βαθμό για όλη τη σεζόν, τελευταία από όσους έχουν σκοράρει, και το ερώτημα αν οι αλλαγές δουλεύουν θα απαντηθεί στο Zandvoort και όχι εδώ.

CADILLAC

ΘΕΤΙΚΑ. Ο Sergio Perez έφτασε μέχρι τον 48ο από τους 70 γύρους, δηλαδή δύο τρίτα αγώνα με δεδομένα, ξεκινώντας από το pit lane μετά από αλλαγές.

ΑΡΝΗΤΙΚΑ. Δύο εγκαταλείψεις σε έναν αγώνα. Ο Valtteri Bottas σταμάτησε στον 13ο γύρο με φωτιά στο εμπρός αριστερό φρένο και ο Perez στον 48ο με σπασμένη ανάρτηση, ενώ πήρε και έρευνα για τη διαδικασία εκκίνησης. Η Cadillac φεύγει για τις διακοπές με μηδέν βαθμούς και μια λίστα εργασιών που ξεκινά και τελειώνει στην αξιοπιστία.

Ο απολογισμός

Κερδισμένοι του τριημέρου ο Norris, που πήρε τη νίκη που του έλειπε, ο Antonelli, που βγάζει βάθρα σε πίστες όπου η Mercedes δεν έχει ρυθμό, και η Racing Bulls, που έφυγε πέμπτη. Χαμένοι ο Piastri, που έχασε αγώνα και βαθμούς χωρίς δικό του λάθος, ο Hamilton, που έχασε μια θέση για ένα δέκατο του χιλιομέτρου, και η Cadillac.

Ο Antonelli πάει στις διακοπές με 219 βαθμούς και 50 πάνω από τον δεύτερο Hamilton, η Mercedes κρατά το πρωτάθλημα κατασκευαστών με 379 και ο Norris, παρά τη νίκη, είναι ακόμη πέμπτος. Πλήρης κατάταξη και βαθμολογίες. Επόμενο ραντεβού το Zandvoort, στις 23 Αυγούστου.

By Stylianos Christopoulos

Ένα τριήμερο που κρίθηκε σε δύο σημεία: σε έναν ασύρματο και σε ένα κιβώτιο ταχυτήτων. Ο Lando Norris είπε στην ομάδα του ότι θα άνοιγε κενό δέκα δευτερολέπτων με φθαρμένα ελαστικά, το έκανε, και τερμάτισε πρώτος με 15.080. Ο Oscar Piastri ηγήθηκε για 33 γύρους, δέχτηκε επαφή από έναν ουραγό και μετά τον πρόδωσε το ίδιο του το μονοθέσιο. Πάμε ομάδα προς ομάδα, με το μπλοκάκι ανοιχτό.

MERCEDES

ΘΕΤΙΚΑ. Ο Kimi Antonelli ανέβηκε στο βάθρο ξεκινώντας με ποινή τριών θέσεων στο grid, την οποία πήρε επειδή δεν επιβράδυνε αρκετά στις κίτρινες σημαίες που προκάλεσε η περιστροφή του Max Verstappen στο Q3. Κράτησε το πρώτο του stint μέχρι τον 22ο γύρο και έφυγε από την Ουγγαρία με τη διαφορά του στο πρωτάθλημα στους 50 βαθμούς. Δίπλα του, ο George Russell έκανε την πιο κοπιαστική διαδρομή του Σαββατοκύριακου: μετά το anti stall στα φώτα βρέθηκε 21ος και ανέβηκε μέχρι την 7η θέση, τελευταίος στον γύρο των πρωτοπόρων. Δέκα προσπεράσεις στην πίστα, από τον Lance Stroll και τον Alexander Albon στον 2ο γύρο μέχρι τον Arvid Lindblad στον 18ο.

ΑΡΝΗΤΙΚΑ. Το anti stall μόνο του κόστισε ένα αποτέλεσμα που ήταν διαθέσιμο, γιατί ο ρυθμός υπήρχε. Και η Mercedes πλήρωσε και τον χρονισμό: έβαλε τον Antonelli στα pit στον 53ο γύρο, τρεις γύρους πριν βγει το virtual safety car. Όσοι περίμεναν, δηλαδή ο Norris και οι δύο Ferrari, έκαναν τη στάση τους σχεδόν δωρεάν. Τρεις γύροι υπομονή θα άλλαζαν το χρώμα της Κυριακής.

FERRARI

ΘΕΤΙΚΑ. Το Σάββατο η ιταλική ομάδα ήταν δώδεκα χιλιοστά από την pole, με τον Lewis Hamilton και τον Charles Leclerc στην πρώτη γραμμή του timesheet. Στον αγώνα η Ferrari ήταν η μόνη από τις μεγάλες που πήγε καθαρά σε τρεις στάσεις (Hamilton στους 13, 30 και 56, Leclerc στους 16, 36 και 56) και ο Leclerc πήρε τον ταχύτερο γύρο του αγώνα, 1:22.000 στον 58ο, μαζί με την 4η θέση.

ΑΡΝΗΤΙΚΑ. Όταν σταμάτησε το κιβώτιο του Piastri, ο Hamilton ήταν δεύτερος. Η Ferrari τον έβαλε στα pit μαζί με τον Leclerc κάτω από το virtual safety car, έχασε τη μάχη της εξόδου από τον Antonelli και βρέθηκε τέταρτος στην πίστα. Λίγο αργότερα ήρθε και το χειρότερο: ποινή πέντε δευτερολέπτων για υπέρβαση του ορίου στο pit lane κατά 0,1 km/h, που τον έριξε πίσω από τον συνοδηγό του παρότι είχε τερματίσει 4.30 δευτερόλεπτα μπροστά του. Προσθέστε και την ποινή τριών θέσεων που είχε πάρει το Σάββατο για παρεμπόδιση του Piastri στη στροφή 1 στο Q3 και έχετε ένα τριήμερο που το χάλασε μόνο του.

MCLAREN

ΘΕΤΙΚΑ. Ο Norris έκανε το σερί: FP3, pole και νίκη. Δώδεκατη νίκη καριέρας, η πρώτη του σε πίστα που είχε κερδίσει ήδη, η πρώτη με το νούμερο 1 στο μονοθέσιο, η 204η της McLaren και η τρίτη σερί στην Ουγγαρία. Στον ασύρματο ζήτησε να σταματήσει πρώτος, η ομάδα αρνήθηκε, και τους απάντησε ότι θα άνοιγε δέκα δευτερόλεπτα με παλιά ελαστικά. Έμεινε έξω μέχρι τον 56ο, πήρε τη στάση του κάτω από το VSC και τερμάτισε με 15.080 πάνω από τον δεύτερο. Ο Piastri, από την πλευρά του, πήρε την πρωτοπορία με μια καθαρή αντεπίθεση στην έξοδο της στροφής 2 στον πρώτο γύρο και την κράτησε 33 γύρους.

ΑΡΝΗΤΙΚΑ. Το ίδιο Σαββατοκύριακο έχει και τη μαύρη του σελίδα. Ο Piastri έχανε τον αγώνα του σε δύο δόσεις: πρώτα η επαφή με τον Carlos Sainz στον 38ο γύρο, μετά η βλάβη στο κιβώτιο που τον έβγαλε από τη δεύτερη θέση στον 55ο. Δύο σβησμένοι χρόνοι για τον Norris σε track limits, στους γύρους 29 και 60, δείχνουν επίσης ότι το όριο δοκιμάστηκε περισσότερο απ’ όσο χρειαζόταν. Και μένει το ερώτημα της στρατηγικής: η McLaren είχε δύο μονοθέσια που μάλωναν στον ασύρματο και επέλεξε να μην παρέμβει.

RED BULL

ΘΕΤΙΚΑ. Ο Verstappen έβγαλε δεύτερη θέση από ένα μονοθέσιο που δεν εμπιστεύεται. Τέταρτο βάθρο της σεζόν, τρίτο στους τελευταίους τέσσερις αγώνες, και η κίνηση της Κυριακής δική του: βουτιά στο εσωτερικό του Hamilton στη στροφή 1 στον 16ο γύρο, στον ίδιο γύρο που πέρασε και τον Liam Lawson. Πρόσθεσε και μια επιλογή που δεν αντέγραψε κανείς, 29 γύρους με μαλακή γόμα από τον 42ο μέχρι το τέλος. Ο Isack Hadjar έκανε τη δουλειά του δεύτερου οδηγού όπως γράφεται στο βιβλίο: στάσεις στους 19 και 42, ίδιο μοτίβο με τον Verstappen, και άμυνα μέχρι το τέλος απέναντι στον Russell με ελαστικά δώδεκα γύρους νεότερα. Έκτη θέση.

ΑΡΝΗΤΙΚΑ. Η Παρασκευή ήταν «πολλά παράπονα», το Σάββατο ο Verstappen περιστράφηκε στο Q3 και χαρακτήρισε το μονοθέσιο μη οδηγήσιμο. Το πιο ανησυχητικό δεν είναι όμως η γκρίνια, είναι η παραδοχή: ο τεχνικός διευθυντής της Red Bull Pierre Waché λέει ότι όσα νιώθει ο Max μέσα από το τιμόνι δεν εμφανίζονται στα δεδομένα του simulator. Όταν ο οδηγός βλέπει κάτι που τα όργανα δεν δείχνουν, το πρόβλημα δεν είναι ο οδηγός.

RACING BULLS

ΘΕΤΙΚΑ. Διπλή βαθμολογία. Ο Lawson 8ος, ο Lindblad 10ος, και η ομάδα ανέβηκε στην 5η θέση των κατασκευαστών με 66 βαθμούς. Μπήκαν στο τριήμερο ισόπαλοι με την Alpine στους 61 και έφυγαν μπροστά.

ΑΡΝΗΤΙΚΑ. Ο Lindblad έχασε την 9η θέση στον 64ο γύρο από τον Nico Hulkenberg, δηλαδή δύο βαθμούς που ήταν στο χέρι τους. Σε μια χρονιά όπου η Racing Bulls παλεύει για την πέμπτη θέση με πέντε βαθμούς διαφορά, αυτό δεν είναι λεπτομέρεια.

ALPINE

ΘΕΤΙΚΑ. Ο Pierre Gasly ήταν ο πρώτος εκτός βαθμών, 12ος, σε ένα τριήμερο όπου η Alpine δεν είχε ρυθμό για κάτι καλύτερο. Καθαρός αγώνας, χωρίς λάθη, με ό,τι του έδωσε το μονοθέσιο.

ΑΡΝΗΤΙΚΑ. Μηδέν βαθμοί και μια πέμπτη θέση που χάθηκε την Κυριακή. Ο Franco Colapinto τερμάτισε 15ος, δύο θέσεις πίσω από τον συνοδηγό του σε ίδιο υλικό, και η Alpine φεύγει για τις διακοπές έχοντας δει τη Racing Bulls να της περνά μπροστά μέσα σε ένα απόγευμα.

ΘΕΤΙΚΑ. Ο Esteban Ocon έφερε το μονοθέσιο στη γραμμή, 16ος, σε έναν αγώνα φθοράς όπου τρία μονοθέσια δεν τα κατάφεραν.

ΑΡΝΗΤΙΚΑ. Ο Oliver Bearman τερμάτισε 19ος με ποινή πέντε δευτερολέπτων για αγνόηση μπλε σημαιών, και το επεισόδιο του με τον Fernando Alonso στη στροφή 3 στον 3ο γύρο εξετάστηκε από τους αγωνοδίκες χωρίς περαιτέρω έρευνα. Η Haas έχει 21 βαθμούς και μοιάζει να έχει σταματήσει να προσθέτει.

ΘΕΤΙΚΑ. Οι πρώτοι βαθμοί της χρονιάς. Ο Hulkenberg πέρασε τον Lindblad στον 64ο γύρο, τερμάτισε 9ος και έβαλε δύο βαθμούς στο κουτί της Audi μετά από δέκα αγώνες χωρίς τίποτα. Για μια ομάδα που χτίζει, η πρώτη εγγραφή στον πίνακα έχει μεγαλύτερη αξία από το μέγεθος της.

ΑΡΝΗΤΙΚΑ. Και μετά είναι το άλλο. Ο Sainz, με έναν γύρο πίσω και σε μάχη με τον Alonso για τη 14η θέση, έκοψε την πορεία του επικεφαλής του αγώνα στη στροφή 3 στον 38ο γύρο. Πρόβλημα του συστήματος όμως δεν σημαίνει άλλοθι για επαφή με τον πρωτοπόρο.

title.raw: Zandvoort's last race and Verstappen's first chance at a win: a sprint weekend, a wet Saturday and a critical fight for pole
title.rendered: Zandvoort’s last race and Verstappen’s first chance at a win: a sprint weekend, a wet Saturday and a critical fight for pole

content.raw:
Zandvoort spent 36 years off the Formula 1 calendar, got back on it in 2021 because one Dutchman was winning everything, and now leaves again while he is still in the car. The Dutch Grand Prix is round twelve of twenty-three and the last one the circuit will host: the contract ends after Sunday and the organisers did not chase a renewal. So the four-time world champion drives his final home grand prix in front of the crowd that built the thing, sixth in the championship, still without a win in 2026.

Winless at his own party

Verstappen has won this race three times and finished second in the other two, which is comfortably the best return anyone has managed since Zandvoort came back, and his three in a row equal Jim Clark's run here. Every one of those wins started from pole. He has never won at Zandvoort from anywhere else, and that is the whole shape of his weekend: the sprint format hands him two goes at a front row, Friday afternoon and again on Saturday, and if he takes neither then the farewell is a recovery drive.

He will run a special helmet captioned "Dankjewel Zandvoort", and he is refusing to be sentimental about anything else. "It's a shame, but on the other hand, the track's still there and I'm sure I will do more laps around there," he said after Hungary, pointing out that plenty of other series still race in the dunes. The feeling turned up somewhere else, in a Viaplay documentary about the race's six-year second life: "No one can take that away from us anymore." A winless Verstappen, at his last home race, in front of that crowd, is not a problem anyone else on this grid wants at the end of a wet Saturday.

The dunes have one rule

The first championship Dutch Grand Prix ran in 1952 and Sunday's is the thirty-sixth. Clark won four of them, more than anyone. The place disappeared after 1985 and did not hold another until 2021, and since it came back the script has not varied once: every winner has started from pole. Verstappen took the first three from the front, then Lando Norris in 2024, then Oscar Piastri in 2025, whose grand chelem (pole, every lap led, fastest lap, win) was as complete as a weekend gets. He earned that pole by twelve thousandths of a second.

Last year also showed what the place does to people who are not on pole. Lewis Hamilton crashed out at Turn 3. Charles Leclerc went into the barrier at the same corner after Antonelli dived down the inside of him through the banking, an incident the stewards judged the teenager wholly and predominantly to blame for. Norris stopped in a cloud of smoke from second with seven laps to go, a broken oil line McLaren took the blame for. Some 305,000 people watched all of that across the three days.

James Hunt's first F1 win, Zandvoort 1975, with Lauda and Regazzoni in attendance. The dunes have been staging this sort of thing for a while.

Back from the beach, same order

The standings did not soften over August. The 19-year-old resumes on 219 points, fifty clear of Hamilton on 169, with George Russell third on 160, Leclerc on 138 and the reigning champion Norris fifth on 128. Antonelli also turns twenty on Tuesday, two days after the race, so this is the last grand prix he starts as a teenager.

The number that matters here is a different one. Mercedes have won eight of the eleven races, and they took the first ten pole positions of the season; Norris' pole in Hungary was the first by anybody else all year. At a circuit where pole has won all five races since it came back, you can see where this is going.

Which leaves the interesting fight behind the leader. Hamilton, Russell and Leclerc are covered by 31 points, two of them in the same team, and Ferrari sit on 307 to Mercedes' 379. Second in this championship is the prize actually in play, and a sprint weekend puts 33 points of it on one table.

The other Red Bull changed hands

If I had a penny for every time Lawson's got called up at no notice to race at Zandvoort, I'd have two, which you could say is a little weird. He replaced Ricciardo in 2023 as the Australian chucked it into the wall at Hugenholtzbocht, the famous, heavily banked left-hander, trying to avoid the fellow Australian who had taken his McLaren seat. He now replaces Hadjar, the Frenchman having reportedly fractured his wrist punching a sand-filled heavy bag in the gym over the break.

So, the car alongside Verstappen has a different driver in it this weekend. As Isack Hadjar will miss the race after that injury, Liam Lawson moves up from Racing Bulls into the RB22, and Yuki Tsunoda, who ended up without a seat anywhere on the 2026 grid, comes back to take Lawson's place next to Arvid Lindblad.

Red Bull dropped Lawson two races into 2025 and replaced him with Tsunoda. Tsunoda lost the seat to Hadjar for this season. Hadjar's injury hands it back to Lawson and hands Tsunoda a car again, and Red Bull have never recalled a driver they moved aside before. Everybody involved has now had everybody else's job.

It costs Red Bull a driver who was actually scoring. Hadjar sits eighth on 68 points, 41 behind Verstappen in a car neither of them has enjoyed. Lawson has never driven the 2026 version of it, and the weekend he gets handed it contains one hour of practice.

One hour, then it counts

Zandvoort has never held a sprint and it gets the fifth of this season's six. The entire weekend runs off a single hour of practice lunchtime today. Sprint qualifying follows this afternoon, the sprint and grand prix qualifying share tomorrow, and the race is Sunday at 15:00 local. A driver who sweeps the lot takes 33 points.

Antonelli. He also owes this circuit something: the last time he raced here he put a Ferrari in the barrier and collected ten seconds and two penalty points for it.

Ferrari, based on track record alone, are most probably not winning this championship. Twelve grands prix run from here to the season finale. We might be waving goodbye to Zandvoort but it's not going down without a fight, offering drivers who perform masterclasses in the wet, such as the home hero in Max Verstappen and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton, a chance to give us a memory that can't be forgotten.

Session times, live and in your own timezone, are on the weekend page, the race starts at 15:00 local, and it is on F1 TV. The question is whether he takes it here, or whether Zandvoort says goodbye to him the way it has to everyone else who did not start from pole. You never can know with Zandvoort.

The Dutch Grand Prix is round twelve of twenty-three and the last one the circuit will host: the contract ends after Sunday and the organisers did not chase a renewal. So the four-time world champion drives his final home grand prix in front of the crowd that built the thing, sixth in the championship, still without a win in 2026.

Winless at his own party

Verstappen has won this race three times and finished second in the other two, which is comfortably the best return anyone has managed since Zandvoort came back, and his three in a row equal Jim Clark’s run here. Every one of those wins started from pole. He has never won at Zandvoort from anywhere else, and that is the whole shape of his weekend: the sprint format hands him two goes at a front row, Friday afternoon and again on Saturday, and if he takes neither then the farewell is a recovery drive.

He will run a special helmet captioned “Dankjewel Zandvoort”, and he is refusing to be sentimental about anything else. “It’s a shame, but on the other hand, the track’s still there and I’m sure I will do more laps around there,” he said after Hungary, pointing out that plenty of other series still race in the dunes. The feeling turned up somewhere else, in a Viaplay documentary about the race’s six-year second life: “No one can take that away from us anymore.” A winless Verstappen, at his last home race, in front of that crowd, is not a problem anyone else on this grid wants at the end of a wet Saturday.

The dunes have one rule

The first championship Dutch Grand Prix ran in 1952 and Sunday’s is the thirty-sixth. Clark won four of them, more than anyone. The place disappeared after 1985 and did not hold another until 2021, and since it came back the script has not varied once: every winner has started from pole. Verstappen took the first three from the front, then Lando Norris in 2024, then Oscar Piastri in 2025, whose grand chelem (pole, every lap led, fastest lap, win) was as complete as a weekend gets. He earned that pole by twelve thousandths of a second.

Last year also showed what the place does to people who are not on pole. Lewis Hamilton crashed out at Turn 3. Charles Leclerc went into the barrier at the same corner after Antonelli dived down the inside of him through the banking, an incident the stewards judged the teenager wholly and predominantly to blame for. Norris stopped in a cloud of smoke from second with seven laps to go, a broken oil line McLaren took the blame for. Some 305,000 people watched all of that across the three days.

James Hunt’s first F1 win, Zandvoort 1975, with Lauda and Regazzoni in attendance. The dunes have been staging this sort of thing for a while.

The standings did not soften over August. The 19-year-old resumes on 219 points, fifty clear of Hamilton on 169, with George Russell third on 160, Leclerc on 138 and the reigning champion Norris fifth on 128. title.raw: One hour practice is rarely enough: Antonelli leads the only practice, Russell steals sprint pole
title.rendered: One hour practice is rarely enough: Antonelli leads the only practice, Russell steals sprint pole

content.raw:
Formula 1 came back from four weeks off and gave itself sixty minutes to work out a circuit it will never come back to. That is the arithmetic of a sprint weekend, and Zandvoort got the fifth of this season's six for the last event it will ever hold. One hour of practice, then parc fermé shuts, then everything counts. Whatever the setup sheets said at the end of that hour is roughly what twenty-two cars raced all weekend.

Kimi Antonelli read it quickest. A 1:12.949 was the only lap all session under 1m13s, and it landed in the closing minutes on his second flying run on softs after traffic ruined the first. He had already spun at the exit of Turn 10 by then, which he explained over the radio with admirable economy: "I don't know what happened there." The championship leader, half a second of drama and then the fastest lap of the day. It is becoming a habit.

The order nobody had time to argue with

Lando Norris ended up second at +0.121, George Russell third at +0.125. Four thousandths of a second between a McLaren and the second Mercedes, which on a Friday means nothing and by Saturday evening meant everything. Lewis Hamilton was fourth and Charles Leclerc fifth, so Ferrari had both cars in the top five before the weekend had properly started, and Oscar Piastri was sixth at +0.659, the first driver more than half a second adrift.

Below that: Alonso twelfth, Colapinto thirteenth, Lawson fourteenth on his first run in the car, Bearman fifteenth, Ocon sixteenth, Tsunoda seventeenth, Stroll eighteenth, Albon nineteenth, Bottas twentieth, Perez twenty-first and Sainz twenty-second.

The session had opened wet. The track was declared as such, damp patches were scattered around the lap, and the early runners went out on intermediates before it dried underneath them fast enough that Piastri was on mediums five minutes in. Rain was threatening again by the end. The Race called it exactly what it was: not enough running, in the wrong conditions, before the part that mattered.

Nobody had a worse hour than Carlos Sainz. Into the gravel at Turn 13, then wide again at Turn 11, floor damage on the Williams, and last of everybody at +3.396. It cost him more than a Friday: the repairs pushed Williams into overnight suspension changes, the changes broke parc fermé, and Sainz started the sprint from the pit lane as a result. One excursion, one weekend gone.

Audi did the clever thing

Look at seventh and ninth on that sheet. Nico Hulkenberg at +0.835 and Gabriel Bortoleto at +1.043, and both of them set those times on the medium compound while the cars around them were on softs. On a weekend with one practice session, that is a team that arrived knowing what it wanted and spent the hour confirming it rather than searching. Audi have not had many afternoons like that this year.

It did not last, which is the cruel part. Hulkenberg's sprint ended after seven laps with a power unit failure, and the car that had looked the most composed thing on the circuit on Friday lunchtime never got to show it.

Eleventh, at his own farewell

Max Verstappen has won this race three times since it returned in 2021 and finished second in the other two. It is the best record anyone has at the modern Zandvoort by a distance, this is the last Dutch Grand Prix the circuit will host, and he ended the only practice session of the weekend eleventh, 1.376s off the pace, after running wide at Turn 13.

Red Bull arrived rearranged too. Liam Lawson was in the second car because Isack Hadjar is out, the Frenchman having reportedly fractured his wrist on a heavy bag in the gym over the break, which is a sentence that should not appear in a Formula 1 season report and yet here we are. It costs Red Bull a driver sitting eighth in the championship on 68 points. Lawson had never driven the 2026 car and was handed it on a weekend containing one hour of practice; he was fourteenth. Yuki Tsunoda, who started the year without a seat anywhere, came back at Racing Bulls and was seventeenth.

Then Russell produced a lap out of nowhere

Sprint qualifying is where Friday stopped being preparation. Russell had topped neither segment: Leclerc headed the first, Piastri the second, and Russell was somewhere behind both. With four minutes left Norris went out into clean air and took provisional pole, and then Russell answered with a 1:11.567 and beat it by 0.041s.

Knocked out in SQ2: Lawson, Tsunoda, Colapinto, Hulkenberg, Ocon, Albon. Out in SQ1: Bearman, Sainz, Stroll, Bottas, Perez and Alonso.

Behind those two, Leclerc was third at +0.055 and Piastri fourth at +0.099. The whole front two rows of the sprint grid inside a tenth of a second. Motorsport.com described it as a tight sprint pole and that undersells it: at a circuit with this reputation for processional racing, Zandvoort's only sprint grid was set by four hundredths.

It was Russell's third sprint pole of the season from five sprint weekends, after China and Canada, and he would go on to convert this one the way he converted China. Sky's framing was the useful one: his title rivals were on the back foot, and one of them was his team-mate.

Zandvoort in orange, the way the circuit earned its way back onto the calendar. Friday afternoon put the man it was rebuilt for sixth on the sprint grid.

Antonelli broke his own Friday

The championship leader's afternoon fell apart before most people noticed. He slid off into the gravel at the penultimate corner during the first phase of sprint qualifying, carried floor damage out of it, and could only manage fifth on his final run at +0.227. Fifth is not a disaster. Fifth with a damaged floor, at the circuit where he collected two penalty points last year for putting Leclerc into a barrier, on a weekend where second place in the championship is genuinely in play behind him, is a Friday he will want back.

Verstappen was sixth, more than half a second off Russell. Aston Martin had the worst of it: new Honda hardware, a scrappy hour, Fernando Alonso locking up at Turn 1 and running wide, and twenty-second on the sheet. He too would start the sprint from the pit lane, for the same parc fermé breach as Williams.

What Friday actually told us

Two things, and they pointed in different directions. Mercedes had the fastest car and the fastest single lap, and they belonged to different drivers, which is a good problem until it is a points problem. And the field was so tightly packed after one hour of running that the sprint grid came down to hundredths, which is not what anyone expects from a circuit whose great criticism is that nothing happens on it.

For the books: Zandvoort's first and only sprint qualifying session, the last Friday of Formula 1 the circuit will ever stage, Lawson's first Friday in a 2026 Red Bull, and a 1:12.949 that stood as the only sub-1m13s lap of the day.

Session by session detail sits on the Friday practice and sprint qualifying pages, with the running order for the rest of the weekend on the Dutch Grand Prix hub and the season's totals on the standings.

One hour to learn a circuit, and the two men who used it best did not end up on the same row. Zandvoort was never going to go quietly.

Photos: Yu Chu Chin, CC BY-SA 4.0 (hero); Danny Tax Creative, CC BY 2.0 (Zandvoort), both via Wikimedia Commons.

title.raw: Russell wins Sprint: A boring Saturday morning, as the sprint format doesn't suit all tracks
title.rendered: Russell wins Sprint: A boring Saturday morning, as the sprint format doesn’t suit all tracks

content.raw:
George Russell started the first sprint race Zandvoort has ever held from pole and won the only one it will ever hold from the front. Twenty-four laps, 30:25.318, 1.360s in hand, and a shower that had been hanging over the dunes all morning arriving at the exact moment he crossed the line. If you were scripting a farewell you would probably not dare.

He got the launch right, led into Turn 1, and had 1.6s by lap 10. The lead moved around a little after that without ever looking like it was in danger. It is the third time he has turned a sprint pole into a sprint win, and given he took that pole having topped neither q1 or q2 on Friday, the whole weekend so far has been Russell finding speed exactly when the timing screens are live.

Leclerc went and took it

The race behind him was better. Lando Norris held second for seventeen laps with Charles Leclerc sitting inside a couple of tenths of the McLaren for most of them, close enough to be a nuisance and never quite close enough to do anything. On lap 18 he stopped waiting, put the Ferrari down the inside at Turn 1 and made it stick. Friday's sprint qualifying had put those two within 0.055s of each other, so the pass had been coming since the timing screens went live the day before.

At a circuit whose entire reputation is that overtaking does not happen there, that is worth more than one position. Leclerc had also started on softs, one of only two drivers who did, everybody else having gone for mediums. Ferrari looked at one hour of practice, made a call nobody else made, and finished second with it. On a weekend where their qualifying pace kept letting them down, their race thinking did not.

The last point, and then a cliff

Pierre Gasly took the eighth and final point for Alpine at +42.510, which tells you how quickly this field spread out once the top seven had settled. Gabriel Bortoleto was ninth at +44.437 and under investigation for an unsafe release, Arvid Lindblad tenth, and Liam Lawson eleventh in the Red Bull.

Three cars had their weekend decided before the lights. Carlos Sainz and Fernando Alonso both started from the pit lane, and not for the ordinary reason: both Williams and Aston Martin changed setup under parc fermé without the Technical Delegate's approval, which carries a mandatory sanction. Williams did it because Sainz's three trips into the gravel on Friday had damaged his floor badly enough that the team wanted the suspension rethought overnight; Aston Martin did the same thing with a car that had already qualified last. Sergio Pérez's Cadillac needed repairs in the pit lane before the formation lap had finished and he came home three laps down.

Nico Hulkenberg lasted seven laps, after a power unit failure ended the Audi that had been the quiet story of Friday practice, seventh fastest on the medium compound while everyone ahead used softs. The one session where Audi looked genuinely well prepared was followed by the one result that made it irrelevant.

What it did to the fight behind Antonelli

Nothing changed at the top and everything tightened underneath it. Antonelli still leads, and he spent the sprint in fourth watching two of the three men chasing him score more than he did.

Russell took the maximum eight and moved to 168. Hamilton took two and sits on 171. Three points now separate them in the fight for second in the championship, and they are not team-mates, which is the part that will make the rest of the season interesting. Leclerc's seven took him to 145 and Norris' six to 134, so the four drivers behind Antonelli are covered by 37 points with twelve rounds left. Antonelli's own lead is 53 over Hamilton and 56 over Russell: still comfortable, no longer serene.

Worth saying plainly, because the arithmetic is the story: Mercedes have the championship leader and the man closing fastest on second place, and they are in the same garage. Zandvoort's sprint was the first weekend this season where that has looked like a question rather than a luxury. The teams' own verdicts on the day are worth reading side by side.

Russell's own read afterwards was not triumphant. "Obviously a great start to the weekend. The Ferraris look fast so it's gonna be tight this afternoon," he told Formula 1. He was right that it would be tight and wrong about who from. Ferrari were nowhere near pole a few hours later. Norris was.

Where it leaves us

For the books: the first and last sprint race in Zandvoort's history, Russell's third sprint win, his third sprint pole converted, Leclerc's soft-tyre gamble paying off with the only real overtake of the afternoon, and rain arriving on the chequered flag rather than a lap before it.

The full order is on the sprint page, the running totals on the standings, and the rest of the weekend on the Dutch Grand Prix hub. The grid it produced is on Crash.

title.raw: Norris clinches pole position: as neither Mercedes improve under worsening conditions
title.rendered: Norris clinches pole position: as neither Mercedes improve under worsening conditions

content.raw:
By the time qualifying began, George Russell had beaten Lando Norris twice in two days at a circuit neither of them will visit again. Four hundredths for sprint pole on Friday afternoon. Then 1.360s in the sprint itself on Saturday morning, from the front, in control. Norris got the last word, and he got it in the one set of conditions where getting it is hardest.

Rain was falling through the closing minutes. Grip was leaving the track rather than arriving on it, which is the version of a late qualifying run where the fast lap is the one you have already done, not the one you are about to attempt. Norris went out anyway and produced a 1:11.163, and Russell's answer was 0.102s short. "I was pushing because every one-hundredth can make a big difference in the end," Norris told Formula 1 afterwards, which on this occasion was a statement of method rather than a platitude. It is his second pole of the season.

A tenth, covering four cars, for the second time in two days

Kimi Antonelli was third at +0.133, crucially behind teammate and championship contender George Russell, while Oscar Piastri took his McLaren to fourth at +0.142. So the top four were inside 0.142s, having been inside 0.099s in sprint qualifying the day before. Two sessions, two days, four cars each time separated by roughly a tenth of a second, at the circuit everyone complains produces nothing.

Piastri's hour is the one worth staring at. He was the fastest man in the first phase on a 1:12.610 and second fastest in the second on a 1:11.641, and he qualified fourth. That is a driver who had the pace for fifty-eight minutes of an hour and did not have it for the two that counted, on a weekend where he has also been out-qualified and out-raced by his team-mate. McLaren get the pole; the reigning champion is not the one having the smoother weekend of the two.

Antonelli, for his part, recovered a Friday he will want to forget. He put a wheel in the gravel in the first phase of sprint qualifying, carried floor damage through to fifth, then came back on Saturday and out-qualified both Ferraris. Third on the grid, 0.133s off pole, at the circuit where he collected two penalty points last year for putting Leclerc into a barrier. He is repaying that debt in instalments.

Ferrari's weekend, in two contradictory numbers

Charles Leclerc finished the sprint second, having taken the place off Norris with a real overtake at Turn 1 on lap 18. A few hours later he qualified sixth, four tenths off pole, behind Lewis Hamilton in fifth.

That is the puzzle of Ferrari at Zandvoort and arguably of Ferrari in 2026. Quick when the race is long and the tyres matter, ordinary when it comes down to one lap on low fuel. If their sprint pace was the real thing, Leclerc starts Sunday from further back than the car deserves, at a circuit where every winner since it returned in 2021 has started from pole. That is not a small problem. It is the whole problem.

Seventh, and within a tenth of the stand-in

Max Verstappen qualified seventh, 0.455s off pole, at the last Dutch Grand Prix Zandvoort will ever hold. Three wins here, all three from pole, and never a win from anywhere else. The fourth row is not where that record gets extended.

The number that will sting more sits directly behind him. Liam Lawson was eighth on a 1:11.733, which is 0.115s off Verstappen, in a car he had never driven before Friday, on a weekend containing one hour of practice, having been called up at short notice because Isack Hadjar is injured, the Frenchman having reportedly fractured his wrist in the gym over the break. Read that as praise for Lawson or as a question about Red Bull's season; either reading is available and neither is comfortable.

At the back, Aston Martin put both cars out in the first phase with their upgraded Honda hardware, Fernando Alonso eighteenth and Lance Stroll nineteenth, and both Cadillacs filled the last row. Carlos Sainz went out in the first phase too, seventeenth, closing a weekend that began with three trips into the gravel and a pit-lane start in the sprint after Williams broke parc fermé to fix the damage.

The grid, stays unchanged this time

No penalties reordered anybody. The starting grid reads exactly as qualifying finished, from Norris on pole to Sergio Pérez twenty-second, with one change: Pérez starts from the pit lane after a rule breach. He was last anyway, so it costs him little beyond the indignity.

Which means the front two rows are McLaren, Mercedes, Mercedes, McLaren, in that order. Mercedes had won eight of the eleven races before this weekend and took the first ten poles of the season; the front row here belongs to the team that ended that run in Hungary. GPFans has the grid with every penalty applied, for anyone who wants to check it against the timing sheet.

Race day

Paddock's own hour-by-hour forecast had the 15:00 start at 19C with a 20% chance of rain, easing to 16% at 16:00 and 14% by 17:00, and it held. Dry, and drying further, the exact reverse of Saturday: rain on the sprint's chequered flag, a wet threat over qualifying, and then a clean Sunday.

That mattered more here than at most places. Water flattens a car advantage and hands a race to whoever gambles best. A dry track at Zandvoort hands it to whoever starts at the front, and since 2021 the man who started at the front has won every time. Norris made it six, though not on a straight line: Kimi Antonelli led most of the afternoon before Norris took it back. The race recap has all of it.

For the books: the last qualifying session in Zandvoort's Formula 1 history, Norris' second pole of 2026, a fourth consecutive session this weekend decided inside two tenths, and a stand-in Red Bull driver within 0.115s of a four-time world champion at that driver's home race.

The full order is on the qualifying page, Saturday morning's race is on the sprint page, the teams' reactions to both sessions are worth a read, and the Dutch Grand Prix hub carries session times in your own timezone. Season totals sit on the standings.

Pole has won every Dutch Grand Prix since the circuit came back. On the last afternoon it will ever get, pole belongs to a McLaren, the crowd came for a Red Bull on the fourth row, and the forecast has taken away the one thing that could have scrambled it.

Photo: Steffen Prößdorf, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.
